new_roles.title: Plant Manager - Manufacturing Operations
new_roles.description:
**Plant Manager – Manufacturing**

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking an experienced Plant Manager to lead an established, mid-size manufacturing operation in Holt, Michigan. This is an opportunity for a well-rounded manufacturing leader to take ownership of the facility's overall business performance, providing strategic direction and leadership while driving operational excellence, profitability, and continued growth.

Reporting to the VP of Operations, the Plant Manager will have full responsibility for the facility's operational and financial performance, including full P&L accountability. This individual will oversee all aspects of the business, lead and develop the management team, and ensure the facility consistently achieves its financial, operational, quality, safety, and customer objectives.

**What We're Looking For**

We are looking for a seasoned manufacturing leader who understands how to run a plant as a business. The ideal candidate brings a strong combination of operational expertise, financial acumen, and business leadership, with a proven ability to translate company objectives into measurable results.

This person will be comfortable leading through department managers, establishing accountability, making sound business decisions, and developing a culture of continuous improvement. Equally important is the ability to balance the bigger picture with an understanding of what is happening on the plant floor.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Assume full ownership and accountability for the facility's overall performance, including P&L, profitability, operating costs, and financial results.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, budgets, and business strategies aligned with company objectives.
* Monitor financial and operational performance, analyze results, identify areas of opportunity, and implement corrective actions as needed.
* Provide leadership and oversight across all plant functions, including production, quality, maintenance, materials, shipping, and safety.
* Lead, mentor, and develop the management team, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
* Provide direction and oversight to the Production Manager and other functional leaders, ensuring alignment across departments and consistent execution of business objectives.
* Drive improvements in productivity, labor efficiency, throughput, quality, on-time delivery, and overall operating costs.
* Identify and implement cost-reduction initiatives, process improvements, and operational efficiencies that positively impact the bottom line.
* Maintain strong customer relationships, ensuring customer requirements are met and issues are addressed promptly and effectively.
* Oversee workforce planning, staffing, employee development, and organizational effectiveness.
* Ensure a safe working environment and maintain compliance with applicable safety regulations, quality standards, and other requirements.
* Direct capital planning and investment decisions, evaluating equipment, technology, and facility improvements to support business needs and long-term growth.
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators, using data and financial reporting to measure results and drive continuous improvement.
* Partner with senior leadership to communicate facility performance, address business challenges, and identify opportunities for growth and improvement.

**Qualifications**

* Progressive leadership experience in a manufacturing environment, with demonstrated success managing an entire plant or manufacturing operation.
* Previous full P&L responsibility, including budgeting, financial reporting, cost management, and profitability.
* Broad understanding of manufacturing operations, including production, quality, maintenance, materials management, and supporting functions.
* Proven ability to improve financial and operational performance through effective planning, execution, and accountability.
* Experience leading and developing department managers and supervisors, with the ability to build a strong, effective leadership team.
* Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to understand financial statements, evaluate operating costs, and make sound business decisions.
* Demonstrated success with continuous improvement, process optimization, and cost-reduction initiatives.
* Strong customer-facing skills and the ability to develop and maintain productive business relationships.
* Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
* A hands-on, approachable leadership style combined with the ability to think strategically and lead at the business level.

**The Opportunity**

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced manufacturing leader to take ownership of an established operation and make a meaningful impact on its overall performance and continued success. The right individual will have the opportunity to influence the business, develop a strong team, and drive improvements across all areas of the facility.

The company offers a competitive compensation package, bonus potential, and a comprehensive benefits program including health, dental, vision, 401(k), and paid time off.

This is an on-site leadership position in Holt, Michigan.

Thank you for considering this opportunity.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan

Experience:

* Plant management: 4 years (Preferred)
* P&L responsibility: 4 years (Preferred)
* composite, paint finish, or similar: 2 years (Preferred)

Work Location: In person

new_roles.title: Senior Consultant, Quality (VP-Level)
new_roles.description:
This individual will serve as an integral consultant with exposure to multiple facets of business operations. The **Senior Consultant, Quality** will be responsible for helping to set strategic direction and operational oversight of the quality function addressing all aspects of GXP compliance.This consultant ensures all internal processes and external partnerships strictly adhere to global regulatory standards, including FDA, EMA, and ICH guidelines.

**This role can be up to 10 hours per week to start.**

 

Elicio (ELTX) is a growing organization based out of the Seaport area of Boston, Massachusetts with additional staff functioning in a virtual based environment from the Greater Boston area and throughout the United States.

 

**Key Responsibilities Include**

 

* **Strategic Leadership:**Develop and execute a comprehensive quality and compliance vision that aligns with the company’s clinical and commercial objectives.
* **Quality Management System (QMS):**Design, implement, and maintain a robust QMS—including document control, change management, and CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action) systems—that scales with the company's growth.
* **GxP Compliance Oversight:**Ensure full compliance across all GxP areas, including Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), Good Clinical Practices (GCP), and Good Laboratory Practices (GLP).
* **Regulatory Interaction:**Serve as the primary liaison for regulatory health authorities during inspections and audits; lead the strategy for inspection readiness.
* **External Partner Management:**Oversee quality at external vendors, including contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs) and clinical research organizations (CROs), ensuring consistent quality standards and negotiating quality agreements.
* **Product Disposition:**Hold ultimate accountability for the review and release (disposition) of raw materials, intermediates, and final drug products for both clinical trials and commercial sale.
* **Culture & Talent:**Build and mentor a high-performing quality organization while championing a "Quality First" culture across all departments.

 

**Education & Professional Experience**

 

* Bachelor’s degree in a scientific or technical discipline (e.g., Biology, Chemistry, Pharmacy) is required. An advanced degree (MS, PhD, or MBA) is strongly preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive leadership in quality within the biotech or pharmaceutical industry.
* Deep knowledge of global regulatory frameworks (FDA 21 CFR Part 11, 210/211, and ISO standards) and experience in biologics or small molecule manufacturing, and parenteral products. Experience with peptide-based vaccines is a plus.
* Proven track record of managing outsourced operations successfully leading organizations through regulatory inspections and commercial product launches.
* Must thrive in a fast-paced innovative start-up environment.
* Exceptional communication and negotiation skills for interacting with executive teams and regulatory agencies.
* Strong risk management and analytical problem-solving abilities.
* Strategic thinking with a "hands-on" approach to building quality organizations and quality systems.

 

**Working Model**

**Weekly hours:** This role can be up to 10 hours per week to start. It may increase or decrease over time.

**Working Conditions:** Busy home office/office/laboratory environment with frequent deadlines and interruptions.

**Travel:** Travel may be required to the Company’s headquarters a few times per year, if necessary.

**Physical Requirements:** Subject to periods of sitting or standing, vision is required to monitor data.

**Work Location:** Hybrid preference but will consider remote

**About Elicio Therapeutics**

Elicio Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: ELTX) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company advancing a pipeline of novel lymph node-targeted immunotherapies for the treatment of some of the most aggressive cancers. By combining expertise in immunology and immunotherapy, Elicio is harnessing the natural power of the immune system with the AMP technology, which allows for therapeutic payloads to be delivered directly to the lymph nodes, with the goal of enhancing the immune system’s cancer-fighting capabilities. By targeting cancer immunotherapies to the core of the immune response, AMP aims to optimize the lymph nodes’ natural ability to educate, activate and amplify cancer-specific T cells, which are essential for recognizing and eliminating tumor cells. Engineered to synchronize immunity in these highly potent sites, AMP is built to enhance the magnitude, potency, quality and durability of the immune response to drive antitumor activity. The Company’s R&D pipeline includes off-the-shelf therapeutic cancer vaccines ELI-002, (targeting mKRAS-driven cancers) as well as ELI-007 and ELI-008 (targeting BRAF-driven cancers and p53 hotspot mutations, respectively). For more information, please visit www.elicio.com.

**About the Amphiphile Platform**

 

Elicio Therapeutics’ proprietary Amphiphile (“AMP”) platform delivers investigational immunotherapeutics directly to the “brain center” of the immune system – the lymph nodes. Elicio believes this site-specific delivery of disease-specific antigens, adjuvants and other immunomodulators may efficiently educate, activate, and amplify critical immune cells, potentially resulting in induction and persistence of potent adaptive immunity required to treat many diseases. In preclinical models, Elicio has observed lymph node-specific engagement driving therapeutic immune responses of increased magnitude, function and durability. Elicio believes our AMP lymph node-targeted approach will produce superior clinical benefits compared to immunotherapies that do not engage the lymph nodes based upon preclinical studies. Elicio’s AMP platform, originally developed at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology has broad potential in the cancer space to advance a number of development initiatives through internal activities, in-licensing arrangements or development collaborations and partnerships. The AMP platform has been shown to deliver immunotherapeutics directly to the lymph nodes by latching on to the protein albumin, found in the bloodstream, as it travels to lymphatic tissue. In preclinical models, Elicio has observed lymph node-specific engagement driving immune responses of increased magnitude, function and durability.

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

This role is part of our Space and Launch business, which has contributed to the nation's space programs for decades by delivering complete solutions from concept to flight. We enable successful space operations with mission-critical technology supporting every step from first launch to final landing, including launch vehicle subsystems, propulsion systems, aerodynamic and interstage systems, and payload protection and deployment. Our high-performance solutions are engineered to operate in the most extreme environments and meet precise mission requirements.

Lead manufacturing operations across Karman's El Monte and Corona locations, aligning machining, fabrication, and downstream processing with business objectives. In this role, you will drive safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and profitability by providing operational leadership, strengthening cross-functional collaboration, and advancing continuous improvement initiatives across complex manufacturing environments.

**Responsibilities**

* Leads and coordinates manufacturing operations across the El Monte and Corona locations, establishing accountability, performance expectations, and operating rhythms for operations managers and functional departments.
* Develops and executes operational plans that align production performance, capacity, and investment priorities with company strategy.
* Oversees machining, fabrication, forming, finishing, and assembly operations to improve throughput, schedule attainment, labor productivity, and profitability.
* Drives operational excellence by implementing procedures and standards that improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and regulatory compliance.
* Champions Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement through 5S, Kaizen, flow and lead-time improvements, cycle-time and setup reduction, Total Productive Maintenance (TPM), and preventative maintenance.
* Analyzes financial and production data, including overall equipment effectiveness (OEE), spindle utilization, and labor efficiency, to manage budgets, inventory, spending, and cost performance.
* Ensures equipment readiness, maintenance execution, and manufacturing capacity align with production requirements.
* Partners with human resources on workforce planning, recruiting, organizational structure, labor utilization, work scheduling, leadership development, performance evaluation, and succession planning.
* Coordinates closed-loop communication and escalation across operations, engineering, quality, supply chain, and program management.
* Manages the administration and performance of subcontracted and temporary labor services.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations management, manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience that includes a minimum of 10 years of relevant manufacturing leadership experience.
* At least 10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including oversight of complex production environments.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of Business Administration (MBA), Master of Science (MS), or another advanced degree.
* Operational leadership experience in precision manufacturing supporting aerospace or defense production.
* Leadership experience in a computer numerical control (CNC) machining environment producing large, tight-tolerance metallic components.
* Experience machining aluminum using 3-axis and 5-axis milling and large gantry equipment.
* Experience with automated or semi-automated manufacturing equipment.
* Experience managing multi-step manufacturing routings and complex production flows.
* Working knowledge of deburring, finishing, forming, welding coordination, heat treatment, and assembly operations.
* Experience building high-performance manufacturing teams and leading Lean transformation.

**Physical Requirements**

* Frequently sits, uses a computer, and communicates.
* Occasionally stands, walks, reaches, or stoops.
* Uses close vision and works with screens for extended periods.
* The essential functions of this position must be performed with or without reasonable accommodation.

This position requires U.S. person status under U.S. export control laws, including U.S. citizens and nationals, lawful permanent residents, refugees, and asylees.

**Benefits**

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off
* Health Savings Account (HSA) with company contribution
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* Company‑paid life and AD&D insurance
* Short‑ and long‑term disability coverage
* Tuition reimbursement

Karman Space and Defense is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

new_roles.title: Director Agentic Talent Programs, Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
The Director, Manufacturing Talent Programs at Phenom is a client-facing, revenue-accountable executive role focused on diagnosing and resolving talent-related constraints for healthcare clients. This position is responsible for conducting in-depth research, building financial models, and engaging senior leadership to drive strategic growth. The Director leads the full client engagement cycle, from initial research to contract closure, ensuring each opportunity is client-validated and measurable. The role offers a competitive compensation package of $250,000–$300,000+ OTE, comprehensive benefits, flexible scheduling, and opportunities for professional growth within a diverse and inclusive organization.

**Job Requirements** 

**Job Description**

Phenom is an applied AI company with a bold mission: help a billion people find the right work. Our platform delivers an AI orchestration layer that sits across the entire talent lifecycle, automating workflows, surfacing intelligence, and deploying agentic capabilities that let enterprises operate at a speed and precision their legacy systems were never built to match.

 
 

We work with the most forward-thinking enterprises in the market, companies that are scaling aggressively, transforming how they operate, and making bold bets on AI to outpace their competition. They range from 5,000 employees to more than one million.

The Director, Manufacturing Talent Programs is a client-facing, revenue-accountable role on Phenom's enterprise team. The Director runs point on strategic account engagements with health systems, hospitals, payers, and post-acute providers. Working directly with CHROs, CPOs, and CFOs, the Director diagnoses the talent-related constraint blocking one of the client's key growth priorities, then designs and sells the Phenom solution that resolves it.

 
 

The Director owns the research and analysis behind each prospect engagement: account research, a documented hypothesis about the client's problem, a map of where that problem shows up operationally, a financial model of what it is costing the client, and a plan for getting the right stakeholders aligned. The Director carries the engagement through the full new client cycle, from first contact to signed contract.

 
 

***If based within 50 miles of Horsham, PA, this would be 5 days/week on-site.***

**What this role is**

* **A revenue-accountable, customer acquisition-focused role:** success is measured by pipeline generated and new customers onboarded.
* **Research and analysis heavy:** the Director builds the account intelligence, financial model, and business case behind every engagement.
* **A role that operates at the executive level:** with CHROs, CPOs, and CFOs as the primary audience.

**What this role is not**

* **Not a demo-led product sale:** the platform walkthrough is a consequence of the diagnosis, not the opening move.
* **Not account management or renewals:** this is new customer acquisition.
* **Not a solutions consulting seat:** the Director carries the number.
* **Not a volume outbound role:** fewer accounts, far more depth per account.

 

**The Talent Constraint in Healthcare**

* **Clinical vacancy caps capacity:** an unfilled nursing line closes beds, and closed beds are patient revenue that does not come back. Staffing is not an HR cost line here, it is a ceiling on throughput.
* **Agency and travel labor is the expensive release valve:** systems that cannot fill permanently pay a premium to fill temporarily. That premium lands in operating margin, where the CFO already sees it.
* **Turnover compounds:** first-year clinical attrition resets the entire ramp, and the replacement cost is a multiple of salary once orientation, preceptorship, and overtime coverage are counted.
* **Credentialing adds lead time no requisition process can compress:** licensure, verification, and privileging mean part of time-to-fill is a compliance problem, not a sourcing problem.
* **Labor markets are local and shift-specific:** a system can be fully staffed in aggregate and critically short on nights in a single market. Aggregate vacancy rates hide the constraint.

**What you'll actually do**

* Research target systems (financials, service line growth plans, reimbursement pressure, and M&A activity) before any outreach
* Build a documented hypothesis on the talent constraint blocking each account's most important growth priority
* Open executive conversations with a specific, researched insight about the account
* Run meetings that test the hypothesis directly with the client and reach a shared diagnosis
* Map the client's current-state hiring process to identify failure points and bottlenecks
* Build a financial model quantifying the cost of the client's current constraint
* Align stakeholders (CHRO, CPO, CFO) to move the engagement through approval
* Build urgency using the financial case itself, rather than deadlines or discounts
* Use AI and LLM tools to accelerate research and sharpen analysis

 

**Core disciplines needed**

**Understand the Business**

**01. Business Intelligence**

For-profit systems file 10-Ks; nonprofit systems publish audited financials and municipal bond disclosures. Read both. Understand operating margin, payer mix, CMS reimbursement pressure, disclosed agency labor spend, and which service lines the system is trying to grow this year. Walk into every meeting already knowing what the business is trying to do.

**02. Hypothesis Construction**

Translate business context into a specific, falsifiable hypothesis about the client's talent constraint before any outreach. Name which growth levers are blocked, and by what, precisely.

**03. Hypothesis-Led Validation**

Run meetings designed to test the hypothesis directly with the client. Ask questions that confirm or disprove the thesis in real time. The goal is a diagnosis the client agrees with, reached together.

**Build the Case**

**04. Process Mapping**

Decompose the client's hiring workflow into current-state swim lanes. Identify handoffs, SLA breaks, and bottlenecks.

**05. Hypercell Design**

Define a discrete, outcome-scoped Phenom deployment tied to a specific talent problem. In healthcare that reads like "med/surg RN, night shift, one metro market, 90-day fill" or "surgical tech, ambulatory surgery centers, three-state region." Each hypercell has a defined job title, location, and job family, a named constraint, and a measurable result.

**06. Financial Modeling**

Quantify the cost of the client's current constraint using the numbers this industry already tracks: agency and travel premium over base rate, revenue per closed bed-day, OR block time lost to staffing, first-year clinical attrition and replacement cost, overtime and shift differential spend. Put a number on the problem before the proposal lands.

**Close the Engagement**

**07. Executive Communication**

Translate operational talent problems into board-level language. Write and speak at the altitude of a CHRO, CPO, or CFO.

**08. Outcome Architecture**

Define success (metric, baseline, target) before the engagement begins. Tie every deliverable to that measurable outcome.

**09. Engagement Orchestration**

Map the buying committee: economic buyer, champion, and any blockers. In health systems the CNO usually feels the problem, the CFO funds the fix, and the CHRO owns the process, while talent acquisition sits a layer below all three. Build alignment across all of them to move the engagement to close.

**Underlying Capabilities**

**Critical Thinking**

Challenges own assumptions before the client does.

**Deep Research**

Synthesizes accounts before any outreach is sent.

**LLM Fluency**

Uses AI to compress prep time and sharpen hypotheses.

**Structured Writing**

Memos and briefs that earn credibility on paper.

**Pattern Recognition**

Applies cross-account learning to new pursuits.

**Intellectual Curiosity**

Genuinely wants to understand how businesses work.

**Data Literacy**

Reads workforce dashboards, reasons from trends.

**Competitive Intelligence**

Knows Eightfold, Beamery, Avature, and Workday cold, plus the industrial and life sciences staffing firms and workforce management incumbents already inside these accounts.

**Operating Mindset**

**Think like a Consultant.** Diagnose before prescribing. Lead with insight.

**Diagnose like a Physician.** Identify root causes, not symptoms. Map the constraint before naming the fix.

**Build like an Architect.** Design the solution before proposing it. Precision over comprehensiveness.

**Communicate like a CFO.** Translate everything to financial impact. Give the executive a one-sentence version of the model.

**What we're looking for**

**Required**

* 7+ years doing at least one of the following: Fortune 1000 consulting in HR; leading a talent acquisition or talent management team; selling recruitment process outsourcing (RPO); or selling client-facing talent technology
* A track record in complex, multi-stakeholder engagement cycles
* Experience gaining access to senior leadership and developing ongoing growth opportunities
* Experience engaging CHROs, CPOs, or CFOs
* Bachelor's degree or equivalent demonstrated capability

**Preferred, not required**

* Health system, payer, or healthcare staffing and RPO background
* Working knowledge of clinical labor economics (agency premium, differentials, ratios)
* HR tech or talent acquisition experience
* Prior consulting, banking, or operator background (super helpful)

**How success is measured**

**Primary**

* **Pipeline generated:** qualified enterprise opportunities sourced and advanced.
* **New customers onboarded:** new logos signed and live.

**Leading Indicators**

* **Executive access:** documented CHRO, CPO, or CFO conversations per target account.
* **Diagnostic accuracy:** how often the pre-outreach hypothesis holds up when tested with the client.
* **Business case quality:** engagements carrying a client-validated financial model.
 

 

**Compensation**

* $250,000 - $300,000+ OTE
 

 
 

**Benefits**

We want you to be your best self and to pursue your passions!

* Benefits/programs to support holistic employee health
* Flexible hours and working schedules
* Growing organization with career pathing and development opportunities
* Tons of perks and extras in every location for all Phenoms!
 

 

**Diversity, Equity, & Inclusion**

Our commitment to diversity runs deep! Diversity is essential to building phenomenal teams, products, and customer experiences. Phenom is proud to be an equal opportunity employer taking collective action to build a more inclusive environment where every candidate and employee feels welcomed.

 
 

We recognize there is more to be done. Our teams are committed to continuous improvement until these powerful ideas are ingrained in our culture for Phenom and employers everywhere!

new_roles.title: Senior Director, Manufacturing Operations
new_roles.description:
**Senior Director, Manufacturing Operations**

*Own the supply chain and CMC project engine behind Nurix's clinical programs and commercial readiness. In this multifaceted role, you will select and manage CMOs, keep clinical supply flowing to trial sites around the world, and drive cross-functional CMC plans from early development toward commercialization, in a small, entrepreneurial environment with broad responsibilities.*

 

**Position Description**

The position is a multifaceted role supporting several areas within the Technical Operations group, including supply chain management, CMC project management, and clinical labeling and distribution. The ideal candidate will be highly motivated and self-directed, with experience and interest in working in a small, entrepreneurial environment with broad responsibilities and opportunities.

 

**The Opportunity**

* Lead the effort to identify, select, and manage Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) for the development and cGMP manufacture of raw materials, RSMs, and DS in support of ongoing clinical programs and commercial products (with finance and commercial teams)
* Manage global supply chains and logistics in support of demand for clinical studies and commercial products
* Working in conjunction with technical teams, provide vendor management support in all logistics and operations to ensure on-time delivery of materials
* Coordinate the design and execution of cross-functional CMC project plans and budgeting for early clinical development through commercial readiness
* Maintain frequent communication with cross-functional CMC project team members and key internal stakeholders so that all parties are aware of current project status, issues, contingencies, milestones, and budgets
* Proactively identify the CMC critical path, risks, and impediments to successful development, and drive the identification and development of solutions to mitigate these risks
* Serve as primary clinical supply chain contact, working collaboratively with internal and external partners
* Manage clinical supply planning and forecasting for study protocols and develop packaging/labeling and global distribution strategies
* Monitor IXRS portal processes, including high and low enrolling site settings, drug acknowledgement, depot and site supply levels, and IMP status of released lots or expired drug
* Coordinate the preparation and/or review of CMC sections of INDs, CTAs, NDAs, MAAs, and other regulatory submissions to ensure timely distribution of clinical trial materials
* Coordinate the process validation programs to support commercialization
* Initiate and manage high-value intercontinental, cross-border, and domestic shipments
* Coordinate the preparation, review, editing, and approval of cGMP batch records and CMC regulatory and Quality documents
* Coordinate the preparation of technical reports, publications, and oral presentations

 

**What You'll Bring**

* BS with 15+ years' experience; degree in Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Pharmaceutics, Pharmaceutical Science, or a related scientific discipline
* At least 10 years of relevant experience in a pharmaceutical or biotechnology CMC/cGMP environment
* Excellent project management skills and the ability to work cross-functionally to develop and execute project plans
* Experience managing US and international CRO/CMOs for the manufacture of raw materials, RSMs, and cGMP DS and DP for programs in development
* Experience with clinical supply chain, including forecasting supply needs
* Experience with cGMP manufacturing and IND, CTA, and NDA filings; thorough knowledge of relevant FDA and EMEA regulations
* Experience in supply chain management, and experience establishing pharmaceutical supply chain systems and networks
* Able to identify and resolve critical issues
* Sufficient technical background and experience to work closely with other technical functional areas
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and exceptional interpersonal and management skills to collaborate with others on assigned projects (including both internal teams and external collaborators)
* Bonus: Advanced degree in Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Pharmaceutics, Pharmaceutical Science, or a related scientific discipline
* Bonus: Experience managing US and international CMOs for commercial programs

 

**Salary Range:** $270,300 - $295,700

*The posted range applies to roles based in the San Francisco Bay Area and reflects local market conditions. Where an offer lands within that range depends on the candidate's relevant experience, technical expertise, and how their background aligns with the role's requirements.*

 

**Location:** Onsite – Brisbane, CA

 

**Fit with Nurix Culture and Values**

* Strong team orientation; highly collaborative
* Solutions and results-oriented focus
* Hands-on approach; resourceful and open to diverse points of view

 

**About Nurix Therapeutics**

*Nurix Therapeutics is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of targeted protein degradation medicines, the next frontier in innovative drug design aimed at improving treatment options for patients with cancer and inflammatory diseases. Powered by a fully AI-integrated discovery engine capable of tackling any protein class, and coupled with unparalleled ligase expertise, Nurix's dedicated team has built a formidable advantage in translating the science of targeted protein degradation into clinical advancements. Nurix aims to establish degrader-based treatments at the forefront of patient care, writing medicine's next chapter with a new script to outmatch disease.*

new_roles.title: Contract Manufacturing Director
new_roles.description:
**Lassonde Pappas & Co.** is a US Leader in beverage manufacturing dedicated to our team members, customers and consumers satisfaction. We remain committed to our small-town roots and rural values. **Hardworking** and **caring** are qualities that make our teams special. Since 1942, we’ve been producing delicious products for our customers across the country!

To provide the best for our customers, we focus on building the best team by creating and advancing an inclusive environment amongst our diverse workforces. If you’re passionate about customer satisfaction, reliable, and committed to being and doing better, join us!

**We value each of our employees’ total wellbeing. To support employees in all stages of their wellness journey, we have a robust benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage options, growth and development potential, along with 401-K, Life & Disability Insurance, PTO, Tuition Reimbursement, Health Fairs, Gym Membership Discounts, and so much more!**

*Pay Range for this position is: $165,000-$200,000 plus annual bonus, depending on experience and geographical location.*

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The **Director, Contract Manufacturing** reports to the Vice President, Integrated Planning, U.S. Beverage and is based in Cherry Hill, New Jersey.

The Director is responsible for defining the role of contract manufacturing within the Beverage Division’s broader supply network and translating business plans into clear external capacity, capability, geographic, and partnership requirements across the U.S. and Canada. This role leads the development and optimization of the contract manufacturing network to ensure the right capabilities, capacity, cost, quality, service, and resilience to support business growth.

The Director oversees relationships with contract manufacturing partners from initial capability assessment and commercial selection through operational integration, product launch, ongoing governance, and continuous performance improvement.

The Director aligns internal business and functional leaders around external manufacturing decisions and builds productive relationships with strategic partners. The role ensures that external manufacturing resources are positioned to support the division’s growth plans, innovation agenda, service expectations, cost objectives, and business continuity requirements.

**Up to 25% travel required**

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**External Manufacturing Strategy & Network Optimization**

* Define and execute the contract manufacturing strategy for the Beverage Division across the U.S. and Canada, translating business requirements into external manufacturing capacity, capability, geographic, and partnership needs.
* Optimize the existing contract manufacturing network by assessing manufacturing capabilities, capacity, geographic footprint, technology, cost, service, quality, and supply risk.
* Partner with Integrated Planning, Operations, Finance, Procurement, and other key stakeholders on make-versus-buy decisions and long-term capacity strategies.
* Maintain a strong understanding of the external manufacturing landscape to identify new capabilities, technologies, potential partners, and opportunities to strengthen the overall supply network.

**Strategic Sourcing & Commercial Management**

* Translate business requirements into sourcing strategies for externally manufactured products, balancing economics, available capacity, technical capability, speed, flexibility, and supply risk.
* Lead competitive sourcing and partner-selection activities, including market assessment, RFIs/RFPs/RFQs, commercial evaluation, supplier selection, negotiation, contracting, and implementation.
* Structure and negotiate commercial agreements that clearly define pricing, capacity commitments, service expectations, quality requirements, flexibility provisions, liability, and business continuity obligations.
* Develop fact-based sourcing recommendations considering total cost of ownership, capacity, capability, risk, and overall strategic fit.
* Establish pricing mechanisms and commercial frameworks that promote transparency, competitiveness, and sustainable productivity.
* Provide financial stewardship of external manufacturing spend through disciplined budgeting, forecasting, cost analysis, variance management, and productivity delivery.

**Supplier Relationship & Performance Management**

* Establish and lead a structured Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) approach for strategic contract manufacturing partners.
* Establish and maintain a robust performance management framework and supplier scorecards for the contract manufacturing network.
* Establish a disciplined operating rhythm with strategic partners, supported by agreed performance measures, periodic operating and executive business reviews, documented recovery plans, and clear ownership of actions.
* Build strategic relationships with key external manufacturing partners to improve service, strengthen capacity and flexibility, accelerate innovation, and identify productivity opportunities.
* Lead supplier and network risk assessments and ensure appropriate business continuity, contingency, and risk mitigation plans are developed and maintained.

The Director owns the performance framework for the external manufacturing network, ensuring that targets reflect the division’s priorities for customer service, product quality, delivered cost, productivity, available capacity, launch execution, contractual compliance, and supply continuity. The role is responsible for converting performance information into timely decisions, recovery actions, and clear visibility of results and risks for business leadership.

**Commercialization & Cross-Functional Execution**

* Lead the external manufacturing workstream for new product commercialization, capacity expansions, product transfers, and new contract manufacturer onboarding.
* Partner with R&D, Marketing, Quality, Engineering, Operations, Integrated Planning, and other key functions to ensure new products and external manufacturing capabilities are launched on time, at target cost, and in accordance with quality and regulatory requirements.
* Ensure effective integration of contract manufacturers into the broader planning and supply network, including capacity planning, production planning, inventory management, service, and supply continuity.
* Coordinate resolution of operational and supply issues across internal functions and external manufacturing partners, ensuring clear ownership and escalating material business risks when required.

**Team Leadership & Governance**

* Lead, coach, and develop the Contract Manufacturing team, establishing clear goals, accountability, and individual development plans.
* Establish the governance, processes, tools, decision rights, and performance standards required to effectively manage the external manufacturing network.
* Ensure accurate and actionable contract manufacturing information is maintained, including supplier capabilities, capacity, pricing, commercial terms, products/SKUs, performance, and contractual commitments.
* Provide business leadership with regular visibility into external manufacturing cost, capacity, service, performance, supply risk, and opportunities, enabling timely and informed decision-making.
* Drive cross-functional alignment and accountability for initiatives and decisions affecting the external manufacturing network.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**

**Minimum Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in contract manufacturing, external manufacturing, strategic sourcing, procurement, operations, or supply chain, preferably within the CPG, food, or beverage industry.
* Demonstrated experience managing third-party manufacturing relationships and complex commercial agreements.
* Strong experience in strategic sourcing, supplier negotiations, contracting, and supplier relationship management.
* Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives involving Operations, Planning, Quality, R&D, Finance, Procurement, and Commercial teams.
* Demonstrated ability to evaluate cost, capacity, capability, service, quality, and supply risk and translate analysis into effective business recommendations.
* Strong financial and analytical acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, cost modeling, and productivity initiatives.
* Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and external business partners within a complex matrix organization.
* Strong leadership, communication, negotiation, problem-solving, and change-management skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in the food, beverage, or broader CPG industry.
* Experience managing a multi-site or North American external manufacturing network.
* Experience with new product commercialization, manufacturing transfers, and external partner onboarding.
* APICS/ASCM certification, CPSM, or comparable supply chain/procurement certification.
* MBA or advanced degree.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Directly manages three employees, providing coaching, development, performance management, and clear accountability for results.
* Establishes team priorities, objectives, and performance expectations aligned with the contract manufacturing strategy and broader business goals.
* Builds team capability and expertise while fostering a culture of ownership, collaboration, continuous improvement, and results.
* Provides leadership across a broader cross-functional network, influencing internal stakeholders and external manufacturing partners to achieve service, quality, cost, capacity, innovation, and supply continuity objectives.
* Leads through influence across a matrix organization, driving alignment and accountability among internal functions and strategic external partners.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORKING CONDITIONS**

This position requires sufficient physical ability to work in a typical office setting; driving a motor vehicle, taking the plane, doing north American travel and occasionally working in the field.

**FREQUENT:** sitting, upward and downward flexion of neck; fine finger dexterity and light to moderate finger pressure to include extended periods of keyboard and mouse use, side-to-side turning of neck, walking, standing, bending and stooping, pushing/pulling, twisting at waist, moderate wrist torque to twist equipment knobs and dials.

new_roles.title: Director of Quality Assurance
new_roles.description:
Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

The Director of Quality, Defense is responsible for overseeing all quality activities, personnel, systems, and performance associated with Defense programs across multiple Karman Space & Defense operating sites. This role provides strategic and operational leadership to ensure all Defense hardware, assemblies, and services meet or exceed contractual, regulatory, and customer requirements. 
 
This position will manage the Defense Quality Engineering organization, supports execution of Defense programs, and ensures consistent application of quality standards and tools across the sector. This leader works in close partnership with the Enterprise Director of Quality to align each site's AS9100 compliant QMS with the emerging enterprise quality architecture and to transition multiple Defense sites toward a unified enterprise certification. 
 
This role is critical in driving disciplined execution, continuous improvement, product integrity, and customer satisfaction within the Defense market segment.

Reports to Vice President, Defense. Functional Partnership with Enterprise Director of Quality (Karman Space & Defense). 
 
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES** 

* Lead, develop, and manage the Quality Engineering team supporting all Defense programs and projects.
* Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, proactive risk management, and continuous improvement across Defense Quality functions.
* Serve as the primary Defense quality leader to the VP of Defense and the Defense leadership team.
* Ensure the quality of all Defense hardware, assemblies, engineered systems, and services produced across multiple sites.
* Oversee program quality planning, including inspection strategies, qualification/verification plans, critical characteristics control, product safety considerations, and risk mitigation.
* Review and approve quality requirements for Defense proposals, contracts, and manufacturing plans.
* Drive effective root cause analysis, corrective action, and failure review processes for Defense programs.
* Ensure each Defense site maintains compliance to AS9100, customer requirements, and regulatory obligations.
* Provide direct guidance to site Quality Managers/Quality Engineers on QMS implementation, audit readiness, and procedural improvement.
* Support site internal audits, customer audits, DCMA oversight, and third‑party certification audits.
* Partner with the Enterprise Director of Quality to align Defense site QMS structures, documentation, and practices with the enterprise quality framework.
* Support the long-term strategy to transition multiple Defense AS9100 certificates into a unified enterprise certificate.
* Collaborate closely on enterprise initiatives such as configuration management improvements, risk management systems, document control harmonization, supplier quality strategies, and enterprise metrics.

 
**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE** 

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or related technical field preferred
* 10 years of experience in aerospace/defense quality roles preferred.
* Strong working knowledge of AS9100, ISO 9001, and Defense customer quality standards.
* Quality Engineering experience with complex programs including design.

**ITAR REQUIREMENTS**

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, certain positions may require applicants to be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

**TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS**

Occasional travel 0-10% of the time.

Karman Space and Defense is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

new_roles.title: Director, Operational Excellence
new_roles.description:
The Director, Operational Excellence, is a hands-on practitioner who supports ESCO sites in deploying the **ESCO Operating System (EOS)**. The person in this role travels to sites to facilitate Kaizen events, take part in key EOS activities, and coach site leaders and teams to strengthen EOS adoption, practice, and results.

Site Presidents and site EOS Managers own and lead EOS deployment at their sites. This role supports them as an experienced practitioner and member of a small central EOS team. The EOS Program Lead owns program strategy and the development of EOS elements, and a peer role owns data, tools, KPIs, and monthly business reviews. This role helps sites put EOS standards into practice on the floor and brings field learning back to improve those standards.

This is a director-level individual contributor role with no direct reports. It works through influence with site leaders and teams. The initial focus is the Aerospace & Defense group, with expansion to other ESCO divisions as EOS deployment grows.

**Key Responsibilities**

***Site Deployment Support***

* Support site Presidents and EOS Managers in executing their annual EOS deployment plans toward EOS maturity certifications.
* Participate in key EOS activities during site visits, such as MDI, Kaizen events, and Gemba Walks, and provide sites with direct feedback to enhance adoption and practice.
* Help sites put EOS elements into practice, including MDI, Gemba Walks, KPI management, action management, P&R, structured problem solving, and leader standard work.
* Provide sites with continued support to improve EOS adoption, sustainment, and results.

***Kaizen and Improvement Events***

* Plan and facilitate Kaizen events with site teams: scoping and chartering with site leadership, pre-event data collection, team training, current state analysis, implementation on the floor, report-out, and 30/60/90-day follow-up.
* Help sites build and manage their CI pipeline so events are selected based on business priorities, KPI gaps, and financial impact.
* Develop site Kaizen leaders and facilitators so sites can run events on their own and meet their annual Kaizen plan.
* Document event results and savings, and partner with site finance to validate benefits.

***Coaching and Capability Building***

* Deliver EOS training on site, from leadership sessions to hands-on floor training for supervisors and team members.
* Coach site leaders, supervisors, and EOS Managers on daily management, visual management, standard work, and problem solving.
* Support site EOS Managers in developing EOS champions and practitioners at their sites.

***Assessment, Tracking, and Feedback***

* Support EOS maturity assessments and certification readiness reviews, including site tours, interviews, and evidence review.
* Monitor deployment progress, action closure, and sustainment at supported sites, and report status to the EOS Program Lead.
* Help site leaders remove barriers, and raise issues to the EOS Program Lead when deployment is at risk.
* Bring field feedback into the EOS program: what works, what does not, and where process guides, tools, and training need to change.
* Share good practices across sites and connect site teams with each other.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Supply Chain, or related field required.
* 8+ years of experience in operational excellence, continuous improvement, Lean, or manufacturing operations, including at least 5 years in a hands-on deployment or practitioner role.
* Has personally facilitated 10 - 20 or more Kaizen events with documented results.
* Hands-on experience practicing and coaching tiered daily management (MDI or similar), Gemba Walks, visual management, standard work, and structured problem solving (A3, PDCA, root cause analysis).
* Experience in a company with a structured operating or business system strongly preferred. Must be a U.S. Person and able to provide appropriate documentation
* Experience supporting deployment across multiple sites preferred.
* Plant or operations leadership experience preferred. Credibility with site leaders and on the floor is essential.
* Aerospace, defense, industrial, or complex high-mix manufacturing experience preferred.
* Lean, Kaizen, or Six Sigma certification preferred.
* Must be a U.S. Person with a valid US passport with the ability to travel internationally.

**Required Capabilities**

* Practitioner first: comfortable on the shop floor and leading teams through hands-on change.
* Strong event facilitation, with the ability to lead mixed teams from operators to executives.
* Direct, constructive coaching of leaders at all levels, including senior leaders.
* Business acumen: connects improvement work to KPIs, EBIT, and customer commitments.
* Ability to adapt to sites at different maturity levels without lowering the standard.
* Ability to influence without direct authority.
* Self-directed and organized; manages a multi-site schedule with limited supervision.
* High accountability for follow-through and sustainment.

**Travel**

Expected travel of approximately **60% to 80%**, primarily domestic, with some international travel to sites in Mexico and the UK. A typical site visit runs 3 to 5 days, such as a Kaizen event week or a site support visit covering MDI, Gemba Walks, and other EOS activities. Candidates should be based near a major airport.

**Compensation Information** 
Base Salary Range: $190,000 - $220,000 USD (Annually)

**Actual base salary offered to the hired applicant will be determined based on their work location, level, qualifications, job related skills, as well as relevant education or training experience.**

Equal Opportunity Employer 
This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights (https://www.eeoc.gov/poster) notice from the Department of Labor.

new_roles.title: Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
**Company Description**

Sirtex Medical is a global leader in healthcare, with offices in the U.S., Australia, Germany, and Singapore, dedicated to improving patient outcomes.

Our mission is to be at the forefront of minimally invasive cancer and embolization therapies. By partnering with physicians, we aim to provide innovative products that enhance patient outcomes and simplify treatments. Achieving this ambitious goal requires passionate and talented individuals who are committed to making a difference. Our flagship product, SIR-Spheres® Y-90 resin microspheres, is a targeted radiation therapy for liver cancer. To date, we have delivered over >150K doses across 50+ countries, significantly impacting patients' lives worldwide. Our success is fueled by our dedication to serving the medical community, maintaining professionalism, fostering a collaborative work culture, nurturing an entrepreneurial spirit, and continuously pursuing innovation and improvement.

At Sirtex, we are committed to creating a great workplace. We offer a range of benefits, programs, and services to support our employees, ensuring they have opportunities to contribute to our success and advance their careers. Join our inclusive community, where you can collaborate with talented colleagues, bring your ideas to life, and advance your career, all while delivering innovative healthcare solutions to patients.

 **Job Description**

**SCOPE:**

The Wilmington plant is the largest of 3 global Sirtex manufacturing site and serves as the principal production site of both SIR-Spheres microspheres and Lava product lines. The Plant Manager is responsible for leading the sites manufacturing operations, engineering, warehouse and product distribution.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

 

* Develop and lead execution of the site manufacturing strategy for both the SIR-Spheres and Lava value streams. Align site goals with Senior Leadership and Corporate objectives.
* Team Performance Management: lead, develop and mentor manufacturing team members.
* Manage production schedules, ensuring resource availability and capacity to meet demand, working closely with the Supply Chain team, using optimal schedules to minimize overall costs.
* Lead Continuous Improvement efforts, identifying process, equipment, product, and other opportunities, that reduce cost, improve quality and safety at the site.
* Full responsibility for developing and managing to site budget.
* Ensure resource and equipment capacity to ensure efficient and reliable manufacturing.
* Set site target KPI’s managing OEE, Labor Efficiency, Scrap, Equipment Utilization, etc.
* Ensure product is built to specification and in compliance with all Quality System requirements.
* Manage the site engineering team to ensure equipment and processes are robust and meet all manufacturing requirements. Manage PM strategy and ensure that execution is completed on time.
* Support the Quality Department, working with on site Quality team members to ensure that compliance with all areas of the Sirtex QMS are being followed. Identify opportunities for improvement and work to implement them directly in the QMS.
* Work in conjunction with HSE/Facilities Department to ensure a safe working environment for all employees and that the facilities is maintained, and compliant with regulatory requirements for both the handling of radioactive materials and medical device manufacturing.
* Manage all shipping, receiving and warehousing activities. Ensure timely material receipt, inventory accuracy is maintained, and products are shipped on time.

 
**Qualifications**

**EDUCATIONAL PREREQUISITES AND SKILL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering or related discipline such as Chemistry or Biomedical field
* 5+ Years experience working in medical device or pharmaceutical industry preferred.
* Prior experience working with radioisotopes preferred.
* 3+ years of site management experience, with 10+ years of leadership experience.
* 6 Sigma Green belt preferred. Experience using 5S and Lean principles is preferred.

The anticipated annual base salary range and target bonus opportunity is $136,000 to $171,000 annually, plus a 15% target annual bonus.

The final position level and compensation will be determined based on non-discriminatory, job-related factors, including geographic location, skills, experience, education, and alignment with the position requirements. In addition to base salary and bonus eligibility, Sirtex offers a comprehensive benefits package, including paid sick and vacation time, medical, dental, vision and life insurance, and a generous 401(k) matching program and other benefits, subject to applicable plan terms and eligibility requirements.

 **Additional Information**

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines

Do you want to be part of something bigger? A team whose impact stretches across the globe making a real difference to the quality of people’s lives. Sirtex recognizes that well-being, financial health, and work-life balance are crucial for our employees to achieve personal success.

Sirtex offers qualified candidates:

* Diverse and flexible work arrangements to achieve the optimum balance between work and personal responsibilities.
* A culture of respect, diversity, collaboration, and innovation fostering inclusiveness and superior performance.
* Attractive compensation and benefit packages which are practical, robust and equitable.
* A commitment to support ongoing professional growth through career development, on the job experiences and training opportunities.
* Challenging work which supports the development of new and better ways to improve clinical outcomes for oncology treatment around the world.
* An unwavering commitment to company values, employee safety and excellence in everything we do.

Diversity drives innovation; inclusion fosters belonging, growth and success. Sirtex believes that it takes multiple perspectives and voices to create a culture and workplace which fosters engagement, teamwork, and employee satisfaction to perform our best and deliver on commitments. We are dedicated to fostering an environment where all employees feel valued, included, and can share their ideas so that we can exceed even our own expectations.

Sirtex is An Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status, age or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Sirtex will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law.

**Company Overview**

DeConna Ice Cream is a leading distributor of ice cream products, serving customers throughout Florida and surrounding states. Our commitment to quality and customer satisfaction drives us to deliver the finest ice cream selections to our clients.

**Position Summary**

We are hiring a Plant Manager for our Tampa location. In this role, you will oversee daily operations, including three delivery routes, the freezer crew, an office assistant, facility upkeep, and vehicle maintenance.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide excellent customer service and support day-to-day branch operations.
* Place stock orders and help ensure inventory needs are met.
* Complete cross-training in delivery, pre-sales, freezer picking, warehouse operations, and office tasks.
* Use computer systems accurately and efficiently.

**Qualifications and Expectations**

* Strong multitasking, punctuality, attention to detail, and customer service skills.
* A clear Motor Vehicle Record.
* Flexibility with start times, which vary by business need and may be as early as 4:00 a.m. on some days.
* Compensation will be discussed at the time of hire.

**How to Apply**

Please apply on Indeed. We will review your resume and contact qualified applicants.

DeConna Ice Cream is a drug-free workplace. Applicants are subject to a background check, Motor Vehicle Record review, and pre-employment drug testing.

Job Type: Full-time

Pay: $42,000.00 - $52,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Employee discount
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Application Question(s):

* Required to Pass a Level II Background Screening for the JLA?

Experience:

* Plant management: 1 year (Required)
* Customer service: 1 year (Required)
* Warehouse supervisor: 1 year (Required)
* Management: 1 year (Required)

Language:

* English (Required)

Location:

* Tampa, FL 33614 (Required)

Ability to Commute:

* Tampa, FL 33614 (Required)

Work Location: In person

new_roles.description:
**PLANT OPERATIONS CAREERS**

Plant Manager

Lead a healthcare laundry plant.

**Where** [City, ST]

**Reports to** General Manager / Regional Vice President

As Plant Manager, you'll lead the full plant (production, maintenance, quality, and logistics) with accountability for safety, budget, and the healthcare customers who depend on clean, safe linen every day.

Why you'll like it here

**Own the plant**

Daily operations, people, budget, and results.

**Lean in action**

Drive improvement with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.

**Lead leaders**

Develop supervisors, maintenance staff, and production Associates.

**Healthcare standards**

Run an operation held to OSHA and HLAC requirements.

What you'll own

* Lead and manage the Safety & Health Program within the production environment.
* Lead, motivate, and develop a team of supervisors, maintenance staff, and production associates.
* Oversee daily plant operations, including production scheduling, labor forecasting, staffing, and workflow optimization.
* Drive process improvements using Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Manage plant budget, including labor, maintenance, and operational expenses.
* Oversee inventory management to ensure consistent material supply and stock levels.

What you need

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, or Business Administration required.
* 5–7 years of leadership experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
* Strong end-to-end understanding of plant operations, including safety, quality, maintenance, and compliance.
* Proven experience managing P&L, budgeting, payroll, and cost controls.
* Strong problem-solving, analytical, and strategic thinking skills.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) and ERP systems.
* Excellent leadership, communication, and organizational skills.

**Physical requirements**

* Ability to stand, walk, and move throughout a manufacturing facility for extended periods.
* Ability to occasionally lift up-to fifty (50) pounds.
* Comfortable working in a plant/production environment.
* Ability to push and pull carts of linen regularly.
* Ability to use required personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hearing protection, and work boots.

**Bonus points**

* Experience with Lean Manufacturing and/or Six Sigma methodologies preferred.
* PMP (Project Management Professional) certification.
* Willing to relocate- GOE flexibility.
* Prior military leadership experience (e.g., Sergeant or above) a plus.
* Familiarity with ISO 14001 / ISO 9001 and GMP standards.
* Experience with manufacturing systems and reporting tools

**We'll teach you:** Our plant network, operating standards, and the support of a national organization.

How we work

Every ImageFIRST Associate lives our four Core Values. These are our required competencies.

**Be Respectful**

Value all we come in contact with.

**Be Remarkable**

Create a positive moment with every interaction.

**Be Safe**

Keep ourselves and those around us safe.

**Be Honest**

Be guided by truthfulness in all we do.

Great work gets noticed

**Everyday recognition**

Coworkers nominate each other for going above and beyond, and those nominations go up in the office for everyone to see.

**All Stars & Council of Excellence**

Each year, Associates who live our values are nominated as All-Stars and earn a certificate and a cash award. Top winners join the Council of Excellence with an additional reward.

Benefits

Weekly pay

Medical, Dental, Vision

Pet, Legal, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance

401(k) with company match

Paid Time Off package

Paid Parental Leave

Tuition Reimbursement

Referral Program

Great company culture

new_roles.description:
Are you interested in working for a company that fosters growth opportunities, community involvement and a team-oriented atmosphere? ClarkDietrich fosters a work-life balance and offers competitive compensation and benefits. Join a team that is STRONGER THAN STEEL℠, by applying to become a Plant Manager at our **Riverside** location.

**SUMMARY**

The **Plant Manager** is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the entire manufacturing facility to include safety, quality, efficiencies, and meeting customer expectations. This includes driving strategic plans that ensure that production goals are met in the safest and most cost-effective manner, while delivering expected financial results.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Direct and manage plant operations for production, maintenance, quality, and shipping and receiving.
* Coordinate plant activities through planning with departmental supervisors/managers to ensure that all manufacturing objectives are accomplished in a timely and cost-effective manner.
* Oversee all aspects of the day-to-day plant operations, including production, maintenance, and logistics.
* Develop, monitor and control plant budget, through active planning and understanding of P&L to ensure financial targets are met.
* Implements cost effective systems of control over capital, operating expenditures, manpower, wages, and salaries.
* Leads the effort and drives Lean Manufacturing tools and techniques fostering continuous improvement within the facility. Acts in a proactive fashion regarding problem resolution.
* Maintains existing plant facilities and equipment; replace or adjust plant facilities and equipment when necessary. Investigate and recommend new equipment or process improvements.
* Actively participated with Regional Sales Management to develop and manage the Regional Operating Unit into a team-oriented environment.
* Establish and monitor overall plant performance for production and quality standards.
* Controls and minimizes labor overtime, premium freight, and repair expenses.
* Provides leadership and training to accomplish the company goals and objectives.
* Incorporates shop floor organization and plant cleanliness among plant personnel.
* Schedules and conducts plant communication which focus on key operative measurements, safety topics and .
* Onsite contact for government agencies, landlords and various other vendors

**SAFETY**

* Strives to improve the plant's safety accident record year after year in creating a positive safety culture for all employees. Conducts safety walks of the facility on a weekly basis.

* Monitors the activities of all employees and provides feedback and discipline to promote a safe workplace.
* Oversee the development and organization of all safety related documentation.
* Ensures and develops all required safety related training and promotes programs to lead safe behaviors.
* Audits equipment and the shop floor for safety related improvements.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Supervise plant staff and ensure employee safety.
* Mentor staff to create a productive and positive work environment.
* Accountable to Establish strong relationships that foster engaging collaborative influence.

Requirements:

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Mechanically Inclined.
* Problem Solver.
* Team Oriented.

**EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor's degree in related field or five years plant/general management experience in a manufacturing environment, strongly preferred.
* Working knowledge of budgets and financial statements.
* Background with manufacturing methods, process improvement programs and procedures required.
* Basic computer experience with Microsoft Word and Excel
* The military equivalent will be recognized in lieu of education and/or experience.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS**

* Basic mathematical skills, addition, subtraction, multiplication and converting fractions into decimals.
* Ability to read a tape measure, micrometer, and caliper accurately.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

* Manufacturing facility exposed to heat and cold.
* Personal Protective Equipment is always required.
* Controlled Noise exposure
* Activity level is high-continuous movement.

**CLARKDIETRICH BENEFITS INCLUDE**

* Full benefits package (Medical, Dental, Vision, Flexible Spending Accounts and Life Insurance)
* 401(k) with company match
* Annual Incentive Program
* Paid Time Off
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Paid Community Service Day

Pay Transparency ClarkDietrich’s compensation program supports the company’s Vision and Values. We offer a competitive compensation, opportunities for advancement and a work-life balance.

With over 30 yrs. in the Landscape Rock and Construction Materials Supplier industry, **MDI ROCK** continues to be the largest family owned Landscape Supply Company in Arizona. With locations in Phoenix, Prescott, Queen Creek, Dewey, and Ash Fork.

**MDI ROCK** is currently seeking a **PLANT MANAGER** for our Dewey Rock Quarry located in **DEWEY, AZ**.

The Plant Manager will oversee all daily operations of the plant from production and manufacturing to ensuring employees meet company standards for Safety, Quality, and efficiency.

**Responsibilities**

* Plan, organize, direct and run optimum day-to-day operations to exceed our customers’ expectations
* Increase production, assets capacity and flexibility while minimizing unnecessary costs and maintaining current quality standards
* Be responsible for production output, product quality and on-time shipping
* Allocate resources effectively and fully utilize assets to produce optimal results
* Implement strategies in alignment with strategic initiatives and provide a clear sense of direction and focus
* Monitor operations and trigger corrective actions
* Share a trusting relationship with workgroup and recruit, manage and develop plant staff
* Develop systems and processes that track and optimize productivity and standards, metrics and performance targets to ensure effective return on assets
* Operate loaders, rock trucks, excavators, and drilling equipment

**Skills**

* Proven work experience as a plant manager
* Working knowledge and understanding of MSHA regulations and possess a strong personal commitment to safety believing all incidents are preventable
* Understanding of aggregate processing and equipment
* Excellent verbal, written and interpersonal communication skills and capable of developing and maintaining good relationships with company and regulatory agency personnel
* Knowledge of ATF and ADEQ laws and requirements
* Ability to create accountability and to lead by example
* Strong team building, decision-making and people management skills

**Perks:**

* Medical, Dental, and Vision after 90 days
* 401k with Employer Match after 90 days
* PTO/PST

**MDI ROCK** participates in E-Verify.

Pay: From $70,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Application Question(s):

* Do you have experience/certification with MSHA?

Do you have experience/certification with the ATF?

Experience:
