new_roles.description:
Description:

The Plant Manager is a senior leader responsible for planning, directing, and controlling activities of a plant to accomplish budgeted operational and financial objectives. Directs all functions at the plant including production, quality control, finance, purchasing, inventory control, manufacturing, engineering, and employee relations. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, data-driven leader capable of scaling production capacity, optimizing labor efficiency, managing complex capital projects, and building a high-performing, engaged workforce.

This role is responsible for the achievement of all operational financial goals. The responsibility also includes establishing and managing operational policies and procedures, creating and maintaining a safe and quality-minded work environment, and fostering the development of a well-trained and motivated work force at all levels.

LALA US Omaha Dairy manufactures yogurt smoothies and pourable sour cream. The facility provides a clean work environment, well-lit, highly automated production facility and career advancement opportunities. LALA US provides a competitive total compensation package including:

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401k with company match
* Vacation and Personal time off
* 10 paid holidays
* Company-paid life, AD&D, short-term disability and long-term disability insurance
* Employee Assistance Program

**Core Responsibilities**

**1. People leadership, talent development & labor relations**

* Recruit, mentor, and evaluate department manager, superintendent and shift supervisors, establishing clear accountability and succession plans.
* Foster positive employee relations, high retention, and strong shop-floor morale through transparent communication, town halls, and recognition programs.
* Manage collective bargaining agreement administration, grievance resolution, and constructive relationships with union leadership.

**2. Production & operational execution**

* Direct multi-shift manufacturing operations to consistently achieve daily, weekly, and monthly production schedules and On-Time In-Full delivery targets.
* Monitor and improve key performance indicators, including Overall Equipment Effectiveness, scrap rates, yield, labor variance, and cycle times.
* Optimize production scheduling, capacity planning, and bottleneck management in partnership with Supply Chain and Materials teams.

**3. Financial management & P&L ownership**

* Develop, manage, and justify the annual plant operating budget, focusing on direct/indirect labor costs, raw material utilization, and overhead absorption.
* Track, analyze, and drive corrective actions on manufacturing cost variances, specifically Material Usage Variance, Labor Efficiency Variance, Scrap/Yield losses to protect margins.
* Partner with Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain to investigate unfavorable material usage variances caused by Bill of Materials inaccuracies, machine calibration drift, or substandard raw materials.
* Conduct monthly financial variance reviews with corporate finance to identify cost-saving opportunities and mitigate inflationary pressures.

**4. Continuous improvement & operational excellence**

* Embed Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies (CILA, Centerline, 5S, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, TPM, SMED) into daily floor operations.
* Lead cross-functional continuous improvement events aimed at eliminating waste, reducing changeover times, and improving throughput.
* Leverage Manufacturing Execution Systems and ERP data to drive predictive decision-making and real-time floor visibility.

**5. Environmental, health, and safety leadership**

* Champion a zero-incident safety culture by enforcing strict adherence to OSHA regulations, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures, and company safety policies.
* Lead root-cause investigations for all near-misses, recordable incidents, and environmental excursions, ensuring timely corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
* Oversee environmental compliance, including EPA permitting, hazardous waste disposal, emissions monitoring, and sustainability targets.

**6. Quality assurance & regulatory compliance**

* Partner with the Quality Manager to reduce Customer Complaints, Cost of Poor Quality, and internal rework.
* Ensure the facility maintains strict compliance with industry quality standards (GMP, & SQF).
* Lead internal, customer, and third-party regulatory audits with zero major non-conformances.

**7. Maintenance, reliability & facilities management**

* Partner with the Engineering manager to achieve the goals on the Preventive and Predictive Maintenance programs to maximize asset reliability and minimize unplanned downtime.
* Ensure spare parts inventory management is optimized to balance carrying costs with equipment uptime requirements.
* Maintain physical plant infrastructure, utilities, security, and building compliance.

**Core Competencies & Attitudes**

* **Unbeatable attitude & resilience**: Maintains an optimistic, "can-do" mindset in the face of complex operational challenges, viewing equipment breakdowns, supply chain disruptions, and cost variances as solvable problems rather than roadblocks.
* **Passion for manufacturing excellence:** Brings genuine energy, pride, and enthusiasm to the shop floor, inspiring teams to take ownership of their craft and strive for world-class production standards.
* **Relentless focus on results:** Operates with a strong bias for execution and goal attainment, consistently driving teams to hit SQCDME targets and protect plant profitability.
* **Hands-on mindset:** Leads from the shop floor rather than behind a desk; actively walks the floor to observe processes, engage with operators, and solve problems at the source.
* **Extreme ownership & accountability:** Takes full responsibility for plant outcomes to engage the team can be focused on results.
* **Data-driven curiosity:** Approaches operational bottlenecks and cost variances (like Material Usage Variance) with analytical rigor, relying on root-cause data rather than guesswork.
* **Action & sense of urgency:** Responds swiftly to equipment downtime, safety hazards, and quality escapes while keeping teams calm and focused under pressure.
* **Servant leadership & empathy:** Listens actively to frontline workers, removes roadblocks for supervisors, and treats every team member with fairness and respect.
* **Continuous growth & adaptability:** Embraces change, challenges "*the way we've always done it"* and encourages calculated experimentation to improve efficiency.

**Core Soft Skills**

* **Multi-level communication:** Ability to translate complex operational metrics into strategic business updates for corporate executives, while communicating daily goals clearly and respectfully to frontline operators.
* **Conflict resolution & de-escalation:** Skilled at mediating disputes between competing departments and resolving shop-floor personnel conflicts calmly and fairly.
* **Emotional Intelligence:** Reads the moral and stress levels of the workforce, maintaining composure during crises like major line breakdowns, customer audits, or supply chain disruptions.
* **Cross-functional Influence:** Builds strong partnerships without direct authority over supporting teams to secure resources and align priorities.
* **Coaching & talent multiplication:** Focuses on developing future leaders by delegating effectively, giving constructive feedback, and empowering supervisors to make independent decisions rather than micromanaging.
* **Active listening:** Creates psychological safety on the plant floor so operators feel comfortable reporting near-misses, quality issues, or process inefficiencies early.
* **Stakeholder & customer relationship:** Represents the facility professionally during high-stakes customer visits, supplier negotiations, and community or regulatory inspections.

Requirements:

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Industrial, Mechanical, Chemical), Operations Management, Supply Chain, or Business Administration.
* **Experience:** 10+ years of progressive manufacturing experience, with at least 5 years in a Plant Manager, Assistant Plant Manager, or Operations Manager role overseeing 100+ employees.
* **Financial expertise:** Demonstrated experience managing a multi-million-dollar plant P&L, standard costing. Demonstrate understanding of managing budgets and controlling costs.
* **Systems proficiency:** Advanced working knowledge of SAP, MES platforms, and demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
* **Methodology expertise:** Proven track record of implementing Lean tools and driving measurable improvements in OEE, scrap reduction, and productivity. Working knowledge of Six Sigma, LEAN and/or Continuous Improvement principles, especially as they apply to a manufacturing environment

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of Business Administration or master’s in engineering management.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Green Belt certification.
* Desirable food/beverage manufacturing plant operations experience, dairy experience strongly preferred

**Work Environment & Physical Demands**

* Split between an office environment and an active manufacturing floor with exposure to moving mechanical parts, varying noise levels, and temperature fluctuations.
* Requires regular walking/standing on the production floor and occasional travel (<5%) to corporate headquarters, conferences, suppliers, or sister facilities.

LALA US is an equal opportunity employer. This document does not create an employment contract, implied or otherwise, other than an at-will relationship.

new_roles.title: Seed Plant Manager
new_roles.description:
**Job Title: Seed Plant Manager**

**Job Summary:** 
The Seed Plant Manager is responsible for overseeing daily operations of the seed processing facility, ensuring production efficiency, quality standards, and regulatory compliance are consistently met. This role manages plant staff, coordinates production schedules, maintains equipment, and ensures accurate documentation throughout all seed handling and processing activities. The Seed Plant Manager plays a key leadership role in driving continuous improvement and supporting the success of the farm’s overall seed production program.

**Minimum Requirements:**

* Farm production and seed processing experience required.
* Knowledge of operating and maintaining seed cleaning and processing equipment (e.g., seed cleaners, carters, indents, gravity tables, aspirators, airlifts, mixers, and scale house).
* Supervisory experience in a production or plant environment preferred.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook).
* Strong knowledge of safety standards and quality control processes.
* Ability to work extended hours, including weekends, as production demands require.
* Ability to pass background check and drug screening.
* Valid Oregon Driver’s License (ODL); ability to obtain a farm endorsement.

**Attributes:**

* Excellent leadership and communication skills, both verbal and written.
* Bilingual in Spanish is a plus but not required.
* Strong organizational skills with attention to detail and accuracy in documentation.
* Dependable, punctual, and proactive in problem-solving.
* Team-oriented with ability to delegate tasks, train employees, and monitor performance.
* Ability to lift and/or move up to 70 pounds.
* Skilled in operating forklifts and other plant/farm equipment.

**Duties & Responsibilities:**

**General Management:**

* Direct, supervise, and coordinate daily plant operations, including seed cleaning, conditioning, treating, and packaging.
* Establish and enforce quality control measures to meet company standards and customer requirements.
* Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local laws, including workplace safety and environmental regulations.
* Develop and manage production schedules to meet deadlines and optimize workflow.
* Provide leadership, training, and ongoing support to plant staff, fostering a safe and efficient work environment.

**Plant Operations & Production:**

* Manage seed receiving, storage, conditioning, and distribution.
* Oversee and monitor equipment performance; coordinate routine maintenance and schedule repairs as needed.
* Supervise bagging, treating, and shipping operations to ensure accuracy and efficiency.
* Maintain precise records of inventory, processing steps, and production results.
* Implement continuous improvement strategies for plant efficiency, safety, and cost management.
* Collaborate with other departments and farm management to align plant operations with overall production goals.

Job Type: Full-time

Pay: $28.00 - $30.00 per hour

Benefits:

* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Ability to Commute:

* Stanfield, OR (Required)

Ability to Relocate:

* Stanfield, OR: Relocate before starting work (Required)

Work Location: In person

DCO Operations

Address:
 
Atlantic City, NJ

Organization:
 
DCO Energy, LLC

Job Type:
 
Full-Time

Posting Date:
 
11/13/2026

SUMMARY
 

* Reporting to the Vice President of Operations, the Plant Manager is responsible for providing management direction and leadership to ensure that the energy facility is operated in a safe, reliable, and economic manner consistent with site contracts, permits, and rules and regulations.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
 
 

* Operates the facility in a safe manner and ensures that a safe work environment is provided to minimize the risk of accidents and injuries.
* Compliance with all company policies, procedures, and commercial commitments
* Implement programs and activities that provide a work environment that promotes effective goal accomplishment, productivity, and morale
* Optimize plant performance through appropriate utilization manpower, equipment, supplies and external support.
* Provide coaching, training, and development opportunities for the team to ensure appropriate skill sets are maintained
* Establish procedures and controls to manage all expense activities to conform to established budgets
* Communicate effectively with the site staff, management, customers, vendors, and outside agencies
* Demonstrate effective management skills in meeting or exceeding facility goals and objectives

 
QUALIFICATIONS AND EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS

* A four-year degree in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering or commensurate experience is required as well demonstrated track record of successful goal achievement
* A minimum of ten (10) to fifteen (15) year’s relevant experience, with a minimum of ten years in a management position.
* A through, demonstrated knowledge of energy facility operations and maintenance as well as management methods necessary to control and improve facility performance.
* Experience managing and supervising employees operating Gas Turbine, Plant Auxiliary Equipment, and Emergency Generators.
* Experience in tracking and reporting Individuals for this position must have good verbal and written communication skills.
* Ability to do reaching, climbing, lifting (up to 50 pounds), walking, and stooping.
* Ability to manage a schedule in a timely and accurate manner
* Ability to handle other administrative duties as assigned by management
* Moderate to advanced MS Outlook Excel, Powerpoint, and Word

 
PREFERRED REQUIREMENTS
 

* GOLD STEAM AND RED REFRIGERATION
* NJ STEAM AND CHILLED WATER LICENSES

 
JOB REQUIREMENTS
 
 
Demonstrated knowledge of all facets of power plant operations. Demonstrated ability to make competent decisions in emergency situations, writing operating procedures and training of other personnel. Demonstrate good verbal and written communication skills. Ability to do reaching, climbing, lifting (up to 75 pounds), walking, and stooping.

Salary Range: 140K-175K annually

new_roles.description:
**Plant Manager Role Description – Händorn**

**Role Purpose**

The Plant Manager is responsible for leading all plant operations at Händorn in a way that reflects and reinforces Händorn’s Core Values. This role ensures safety, quality, efficiency, profitability, and scalability while modeling **Learning-Led Excellence**, **Make it Easier for Someone Else**, **Thinking Together, Win to Together**, and being **Determined to Succeed**.

The Plant Manager serves as the operational backbone of the company and is expected to serve on the Leadership Team, translating company strategy into disciplined execution while building a strong culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and teamwork.

This role is critical to supporting Händorn’s growth objectives as production leadership transitions and capacity expands.

**Key Outcomes (What Success Looks Like)**

* Safe, efficient, and scalable plant operations grounded in continuous learning
* Consistent on-time delivery and high-quality output that makes work easier downstream
* Clearly defined processes, standards, and accountability that reduce friction
* Strong team engagement, collaboration, and succession planning
* Accurate financial, production, and operational reporting
* Continuous improvement in cost, throughput, quality, and team capability

**Core Responsibilities**

**1. Leadership, Culture & Core Values**

* Lead by example, consistently modeling Händorn’s core values in decisions and behaviors
* Maintain and develop the management team through coaching, feedback, and accountability
* Set and reinforce clear expectations so teams can succeed without confusion
* Foster a culture of curiosity, learning, and improvement—treating challenges as opportunities
* Encourage collaboration across departments, breaking down silos and aligning goals
* Resolve department conflicts constructively and respectfully
* Act as Chief Change Implementer, helping teams navigate change with clarity and confidence
* Build stability and trust through integrity, transparency, and follow-through

**2. Operations & Production Management**

* Oversee daily plant operations, production scheduling, and capacity planning
* Increase throughput while maintaining safety, quality, and team sustainability
* Monitor and act on measurables related to safety, quality, delivery, cost, and efficiency
* Ensure shop layout, workflow, and material organization support ease of execution
* Manage fabrication employees and shop leadership with clear priorities and support
* Oversee maintenance, machine integration, and equipment utilization
* Serve as the final operational checkpoint before work enters production, ensuring accuracy and readiness

**3. Quality, Safety & Compliance**

* Champion a safety-first mindset and enforce safety protocols and health standards
* Monitor quality control reporting and address issues promptly and thoroughly
* Build systems that prevent errors rather than relying on heroics
* Ensure internal controls, documentation, and regulatory compliance
* Proactively identify and manage operational risks to the company

**4. Financial & Business Management**

* Own plant-level financial awareness, including cost control and profitability drivers
* Lead budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting in partnership with leadership
* Identify cost-reduction opportunities without sacrificing quality or safety
* Approve purchasing within established limits, ensuring thoughtful and timely decisions
* Manage vendor relationships and lead commodity-level cost negotiations
* Support capital investment decisions with clear ROI and long-term impact analysis

**5. Planning, Measurables & Continuous Improvement**

* Create, maintain, and continuously refine operational measurables and scorecards and measurables
* Monitor capacity, inventory levels, and material flow to reduce bottlenecks
* Standardize processes and documentation to make work easier for others
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives rooted in data and learning
* Implement and support new software, systems, and tools effectively
* Research industry trends, equipment, and best practices to keep Händorn competitive

**6. Cross-Functional Coordination**

* Think together with engineering, project management, sales, and finance to win together
* Ensure accurate and complete documentation including BOMs, work orders, drawings, and revisions
* Coordinate delivery planning to meet customer expectations consistently
* Communicate changes clearly, early, and consistently across teams
* Support internal and external customer satisfaction through proactive collaboration

**7. People Development & HR Support**

* Support hiring, staffing levels, and structured onboarding
* Drive training, cross-training, and succession planning to build bench strength
* Monitor performance and provide timely, constructive feedback
* Maintain high employee engagement through clarity, respect, and shared ownership
* Promote teamwork, accountability, and pride in workmanship

**Required Skills & Experience**

**Minimum Requirements**

* **10+ years in manufacturing operations**
* **5–8+ years in architectural millwork, cabinetry, or commercial casework**
* **5+ years leading supervisors or department managers**
* Experience managing **custom, project-based production**
* Strong familiarity with **CNC-driven manufacturing environments**
* Demonstrated experience improving throughput in a high-mix environment
* Proven Lean / Continuous Improvement implementation
* OSHA and safety program leadership experience
* ERP/MRP manufacturing systems experience
* Budgeting and capital planning experience, with focus on forecasting and cost control
* Data-driven mindset with experience managing measurables and operational measurables
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Construction Management, or related field, or equivalent industry experience
* Strong leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills
* Ability to delegate effectively while maintaining accountability
* Demonstrated alignment with Händorn’s core values

**Preferred**

* AWI standards familiarity
* Experience scaling plant capacity through systems, people, and process improvement
* Experience leading 15+ employees

**Key Interfaces**

* CEO and Leadership Team
* Department Managers and Supervisors
* Engineering, Project Management, Sales, and Finance
* HR and Administrative Support
* Vendors, Suppliers, and Logistics Partners

**Measures of Performance**

* Safety performance and incident rates
* On-time delivery and throughput
* Quality measurables, rework, and scrap reduction
* Cost control and budget adherence
* Employee engagement, retention, and development
* Process standardization, scalability, and continuous improvement results

Job Type: Full-time

Pay: $75,000.00 - $100,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off

Experience:

* Manufacturing: 10 years (Preferred)
* Architectural Millwork, Cabinetry, or Commercial Casework: 5 years (Preferred)
* Leadership: 5 years (Required)

Work Location: In person

new_roles.description:
**For nearly 100 years, Everbrite** **has been providing innovative visual identification, outdoor signage, indoor signs & displays, menu systems, architectural & drive-thru elements, electronic displays, scoreboards, and LED lighting solutions to leading companies throughout the world.**

As an industry leader, our mission is to understand and exceed our customers’ needs. To that end we believe:

* Our employees are our greatest strength.
* Each product we develop and service is reflective of the great people we hire.

This role offers the opportunity to contribute to a growing and dynamic work environment. If this is the environment for you, we would love to talk to you about a career with Everbrite.

**Position Summary:**

The Plant Manager will direct, manage, and coordinate all areas of production, materials, engineering, and related services through managers, supervisors and lead people to achieve timely production of quality products at the most economical cost and in the proper quantities, ensuring on-time delivery. Responsible for the operational improvements of all aspects of the plant production and process controls. Responsible for facility maintenance (building and grounds) and equipment, as well as supervising Environmental/Safety/Quality personnel. Organize and lead the Continuous Improvement Program to include cost savings projects and administration and documentation of the Idea program. Work with management in planning and implementing Quality/Continuous Improvement (QCI) activities.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Direct and manage all production-related departments (including maintenance and prototype) in general administration and enforcement of company rules and regulations. This includes employee selection and development, employee relations, discipline, safety, etc.
* Plan, organize and coordinate manufacturing procedures and operations to accomplish objectives in accordance with production and delivery schedules, skills and manufacturing capacities to maintain profitable operation.
* Provide technical expertise in terms of manufacturing, materials, lead-time, equipment workflow, resources to manufacture new products or improve manufacturing efficiency of existing products, while maintaining or improving quality.
* Control labor and material variances through adequate supervision and cost monitoring.
* Moderate production meetings to assist in planning and making recommendations on matters having to do with manufacturing operations.
* Manage finished goods inventory and warehouse facilities.
* Remain abreast of new manufacturing technology, equipment processes and management techniques through publications, seminars, workshops, or attending related shows or exhibits.
* Conduct timely performance reviews of direct reports, recommending training, changes of wage or status, updating or creating job descriptions, and setting agreeable goals and objectives.
* Maintain an efficient and skilled workforce through formal and informal training and work skill enhancement in order to meet projected workload, advancements in technology and compliance with Quality System requirements.
* Prepare reports and make presentations to members of plant, division and/or corporate management related to production performance.
* Ensure equipment receives regular preventative maintenance and that the plant’s housekeeping exceeds safety standards.
* Develop the most efficient way to employ manpower, machines, materials, information, and energy to manufacture the product or provide a service.
* Develop management control systems and processes to measure productivity, i.e., OEE (Overall Equipment Efficiency), OTD (On Time Delivery), etc.
* Analyze cycle times to improve/increase productivity. Design/improve production planning and control systems and resolve production process problems.
* Study material flow, operations sequence and recommend/implement appropriate changes.
* Evaluate the effects of product design changes.
* Design/improve manufacturing process methods to assure product quality. Assist in setting goals, and planning projects that will meet corporate and plant Quality/CI objectives.
* Oversee the administration of the Ideas program and cost savings projects.
* Assist management in maintaining the Plant within environmental and quality performance regulations.
* Key member of the Safety Committee.
* Assure all plant emergency systems are functioning properly.
* Responsible for developing, communicating, improving, and adhering to safety policies in all work environments and other areas.
* Participate in financial planning, cost/benefit analysis for building, grounds and plant equipment.
* Continue Quality/CI self-education training, Grand Kaizen and participating in other skill enhancement activities.
* Assure that plant personnel are trained and help develop their Quality/CI skills. Conduct Quality/CI skill enhancement sessions.
* Help develop Team Members’ skills; CI, problem solving, Quality, and provide leadership.
* Supervise maintenance department and plan work for maintenance employees, assuring Preventative Maintenance processes are followed. Assist and provide maintenance resources for CI/Kaizen projects.
* Work closely with equipment suppliers, plant staff, and Continuous Improvement Specialist to assure the successful operation of the plant.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Educational Requirements / Experience:**

* Business, manufacturing or engineering-related degree or equivalent years of related work experience. A formal apprenticeship or courses/seminars in supervision would be considered a plus.
* Minimum of 5 years of related production management experience from a similar type manufacturing company or 12 years of management experience from a non-related type of manufacturing.
* Minimum of 5 years’ continuous improvement experience with Lean Enterprise and/or Toyota Production System as demonstrated through participation in and leadership of CI events/projects.
* Possess Quality/CI program certification and/or demonstrate competency.

**Additional Attributes:**

* Excellent verbal communication skills, as well as the ability to utilize Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and E-mail to effectively communicate with others.
* Create presentations as necessary.
* Ability to work with a variety of individuals at all levels.
* Perform basic data analyses as required.
* Create charts, templates, flow maps for standards and clear communication of information.
* Self-motivated.
* Work independently and communicate effectively with others.
* Excellent Project Management skills.
* Lead and manage a team to bring closure to projects.
* Systematic and analytical approach to problem solving.
* Proficient with the concepts and tools of Quality Tools and Lean Manufacturing used in Kaizen analysis.
* Proficient with Value Stream Mapping tools.
* Apply Lean manufacturing tools and train plant associates on various lean tools and techniques, as well as become the resource “expert” for lean methodologies.
* Track and report plant improvement progress.
* Work with team members and supervisors to sustain results by monitoring 30, 60 and 90 day follow up reports.
* Strong leadership and organizational skills with aptitude for facilitating teams and/or activities. Effectively lead a team through an entire event – from training through report-out.
* Show initiative, desire to drive change and motivation to exceed expectations.
* Skilled in statistical knowledge and the ability to apply statistics to product and process improvement projects.
* Competent in Lean principles, including Waste elimination, Pull systems, Kanban, Visual workspace, One Piece Flow, Flow Production, Set-Up Reduction, Standardized Work, Variation Reduction, Error Proofing, Total Productive Maintenance, Ergonomics, Problem Solving, and Level Loading.

**Equal Opportunity Statement:** Everbrite, LLC provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

new_roles.title: Director of Operations - Aiken, SC
new_roles.description:
**Job Overview**
----------------

The Director of Operations is responsible for the activities of manufacturing, purchasing, quality, planning (supply chain), and project management of the organization and aids in formulating and administering organization policies.

#LI-SL1

**A Day In The Life**
---------------------

Every day at Hubbell is different and you’ll contribute in many ways. On any given day, you’ll make a difference by:

* Participating in formulating/administering company policies and developing long range goals/objectives.
* Directing/coordinating activities of the responsible departments on a day-to-day basis to ensure that daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual objectives are met.
* Ensuring internal auditing for compliance with the ISO standards applicable.
* Driving cost reduction (productivity) planning and execution in accordance with the financial plan.
* Providing authorization for funds to ensure responsible fiduciary spending in accordance with financial policies.
* Reviewing/analyzing activities related to costs, operations, CAPEX, and forecast data to determine progress toward financial goals and objectives and considering the long-range impact of growing the business and adjusting actions to ensure compliance.
* Overseeing the budget/forecast processes as well as ongoing monitoring to ensure compliance.
* Conferring with other senior personnel to review achievements and discuss required changes in goals or objectives resulting from current status/conditions.
* Developing plans and executing actions to meet the decision upon actions.
* Providing oversight and coordination to other business in Operations related matters to drive consistency among the businesses.
* Participating in due diligence process as requested.
* Developing succession planning strategies in coordination with HR to ensure continuation of leadership/individual contributor roles going forward.

**What will help you thrive in this role?**
-------------------------------------------

* Bachelor’s Degree in Business Management, Industrial Engineering, or related field
* Master’s Degree in Business Administration (required)
* 20+ years of relevant operations experience (required)
* 20+ years of experience as a Senior Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or a similar role, preferably in a heavy manufacturing environment with multi-site responsibility
* 10+ years of experience with TPM and SAP
* Welding, Fabricating, Warehouse & Logistics experience
* Operational Excellence or Lean Certification
* Strong knowledge of Lean Manufacturing
* Staff development and engagement skills
* Bi-lingual Spanish/English preferred

**Hubbell Incorporated**

Hubbell creates critical infrastructure solutions that power our customers, communities, people and the planet. Our company is strategically aligned around enabling grid modernization and electrification. As more products plug in to an aging grid, Hubbell solutions enable the transition to a more reliable, resilient and efficient energy infrastructure. Founded in 1888 our innovation has made us a leading global manufacturer of high quality electrical and utility solutions enabling customers to operate critical infrastructure reliably and efficiently.

The company operates in two segments. Hubbell Utility Solutions (HUS) enable the grid to conduct, communicate and control energy across utility applications and Hubbell Electrical Solutions (HES) are essential to managing power across a wide range of industries and applications. Our vertical market solutions can be applied to markets including Data Centers, Renewables, Commercial Buildings, Industrial, Telecom and Transportation. Supporting both of our business segments is our corporate and Hubbell Unified Business Solutions teams that provide consistent process, tools technologies across our businesses.

We are committed to operating sustainably and ethically while promoting an inclusive and supportive culture for our people to grow and develop in their careers. Our employees proudly work and serve our communities from our headquarters in Shelton, CT, across the United States and around the globe.

**Hubbell Utility Solutions**

Hubbell Utility Solutions (HUS) enable the grid to conduct, communicate and control energy across utility applications. HUS provides the critical components that allow the grid to reliably transmit and distribute energy, as well as the communications and controls technologies to make the grid smarter and more flexible.

Hubbell Incorporated, its subsidiaries and affiliates, is an EO Employer AA: M/F/Veteran/Disability. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other protected class.

The above summary of position responsibilities and requirements is not intended, and should not be construed, to be an exhaustive list of duties, skills, efforts, physical requirements, or working conditions associated with the position. It is intended to be an accurate reflection of those principal position elements essential for making decisions related to position performance, employee development, and compensation.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Quality & QMS
new_roles.description:
**Job Overview:**

The Senior Manager, Quality & QMS is responsible for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continuously improving the Quality Management System (QMS) for Intech’s medical device manufacturing operations.

This position provides senior-level leadership for all site quality activities, including production quality, nonconformance management, CAPA, internal and external audits, supplier quality, document and record control, quality metrics, and continuous improvement. A primary responsibility of the role will be to lead the organization in developing and implementing an effective QMS and preparing the site for ISO 9001 certification.

This position will serve as the primary quality leader for the site and will work closely with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Product Development, and other functional leaders to ensure that quality is integrated into the business and manufacturing processes rather than operating as a separate inspection function. This role is a hands-on position and will operate strategically while also working directly with manufacturing personnel to establish practical, sustainable quality processes.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Own the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the site's Quality Management System.
* Lead the organization through its ISO 9001 readiness and certification process.
* Establish and maintain quality policies, procedures, work instructions, forms, records, and other QMS documentation.
* Establish effective document and record control processes.
* Develop quality objectives, metrics, and management-review processes.
* Ensure QMS processes are understood, implemented, and effective across the organization.
* Identify gaps, risks, and opportunities for improvement and develop practical plans to address them.
* Provide leadership for quality throughout the manufacturing process.
* Establish appropriate inspection, testing, sampling, and process-control requirements.
* Partner with Operations and Engineering to identify and eliminate sources of variation and defects.
* Monitor production quality performance and trends.
* Lead efforts to reduce scrap, rework, defects, and recurring quality issues.
* Ensure appropriate controls are in place for nonconforming product(s), product identification, traceability, and inspection status.
* Support process changes, equipment changes, product introductions, and manufacturing improvements from a quality perspective.
* Own and continuously improve the site's CAPA and nonconformance processes.
* Lead investigations into significant quality issues and recurring nonconformances.
* Establish effective root-cause analysis and corrective-action practices.
* Ensure corrective actions address systemic causes and are implemented and verified for effectiveness.
* Monitor CAPA and NCR trends to identify broader process and systemic issues.
* Establish appropriate escalation of significant quality risks to site leadership.
* Develop and manage the internal audit program.
* Conduct or oversee internal QMS and process audits.
* Coordinate customer, certification, surveillance, and other external audits.
* Serve as the primary quality contact during external audits.
* Ensure audit findings are appropriately investigated, corrected, and closed.
* Build an organization that is continuously audit-ready rather than preparing only immediately before an audit.
* Establish and maintain supplier quality processes.
* Develop supplier qualification, evaluation, monitoring, and re-evaluation practices.
* Establish supplier quality expectations in partnership with Supply Chain and Operations.
* Monitor supplier quality performance and trends.
* Lead or support supplier corrective actions.
* Participate in supplier selection and qualification activities as appropriate.
* Address recurring supplier issues through effective root-cause analysis and corrective action.
* Establish meaningful quality metrics and dashboards.
* Monitor trends in NCRs, CAPAs, audits, supplier performance, scrap, rework, customer issues, and other relevant indicators.
* Translate quality data into actionable improvement initiatives.
* Provide regular quality performance updates to leadership.
* Use structured problem-solving and continuous-improvement methodologies to improve processes and reduce risk.
* Develop strong working relationships with employees at all levels of the organization.
* Partner closely with manufacturing personnel to solve problems at the source.
* Provide quality leadership, coaching, and training.
* Establish clear expectations for quality ownership throughout the organization.
* Promote a culture of prevention, accountability, disciplined problem-solving, and continuous improvement.
* Communicate quality risks clearly and objectively to leadership.

*Management reserves the right to change job duties and responsibilities at any time. Therefore, this job description is not designed to cover every requirement of the job.*

**Education and Work Experience Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Quality, Engineering, Manufacturing, Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent relevant experience.
* 7+ years of progressive experience in quality, quality systems, manufacturing quality, or a related discipline.
* Demonstrated experience implementing, managing, or significantly improving a Quality Management System.
* Strong working knowledge of ISO 9001.
* Must have demonstrated experience taking an organization through ISO 9001 certification.
* Demonstrated experience with CAPA, nonconformance management, root-cause analysis, and corrective action.
* Experience leading internal and external audits.
* Experience working directly in a manufacturing environment.
* Experience with supplier quality and supplier corrective actions.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills.
* Ability to work effectively with both production personnel and senior leadership.
* Ability to establish structure and processes in an environment where the QMS is still developing.
* Medical device manufacturing experience preferred.
* ISO 9001 Lead Auditor or Internal Auditor training/certification preferred.
* ASQ certification such as CQA, CQE, or CMQ/OE.
* Experience with statistical process control, process capability, risk management, or other quality engineering tools.
* Lean Six Sigma or other continuous-improvement experience a plus.
* Familiarity with applicable medical-device quality and regulatory requirements a plus

**Physical Demands and Work Environment:**

* Ability to maintain regular, punctual attendance consistent with company policies
* Must occasionally lift, carry and/or move up to 25 lbs.
* Occasionally required to stand, walk, bend, and constantly sit for extended periods
* Must be able to talk, listen and speak clearly on the telephone
* Continually required to read, write, and type
* Occasional exposure to heat or cold (non-weather) environments
* Occasionally required to use hand/arm movements such as grasping, reaching, pulling

new_roles.title: Senior Manager of Production
new_roles.description:
Gwynedd Manufacturing is seeking a hands-on Senior Manager of Production with a strong CNC machining background to lead day-to-day operations in a high-precision environment. This role is ideal for someone who has progressed through the ranks—from the shop floor into leadership—and is ready to step into a broader operational role.

The ideal candidate brings deep, practical knowledge of CNC machining (mills, lathes, EDM) and thrives in a fast-paced, high-tolerance manufacturing setting. This is not a purely strategic role—this leader will be actively engaged on the floor, driving performance, mentoring teams, and continuously improving processes.

Key Responsibilities:

* Lead daily plant operations with a strong presence on the manufacturing floor, ensuring output, quality, and efficiency targets are met
* Direct oversight of machining operations including CNC mills, lathes, and EDM, ensuring optimal machine utilization and performance
* Manage and develop a team of supervisors, leads, and machinists (50–100+ employees)
* Serve as a technical resource and mentor, supporting setup, programming, and troubleshooting when needed
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on cycle time reduction, scrap reduction, and process standardization
* Partner closely with Engineering and Quality to ensure tight tolerance requirements and manufacturability of parts
* Own production scheduling, workflow optimization, and labor planning to meet customer demand
* Establish and reinforce shop floor accountability, KPIs, and standard work practices
* Maintain a safe, compliant, and disciplined manufacturing environment
* Support new product introductions and prototype builds with a strong understanding of machining constraints
* Overseeing multiple departments withing the manufacturing space.

Qualifications:

* 5+ years of progressive manufacturing experience, with clear growth from hands-on machining into leadership
* Strong CNC background required (setup, programming, and/or machining experience with mills, lathes, EDM)
* Prior experience in roles such as Machine Shop Manager, Manufacturing Manager, or Plant Manager
* Proven ability to lead teams in a high-precision, tight-tolerance environment
* Deep understanding of machining processes, tooling, fixturing, and production workflows
* Experience driving continuous improvement on the shop floor (Lean, process optimization, etc.)
* Comfortable being hands-on and highly visible in daily operations, not just managing from an office
* Strong leadership and communication skills with the ability to develop talent from within
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related field preferred, but equivalent hands-on experience strongly valued

Physical and Work Environment Requirements: 
This position is based in a manufacturing environment and may require the following over extended periods of time up to a full 8-hour work shift (excluding lunch and breaks): stand, walk, sit, squat or bend, kneel and rise, lift, carry, push, or pull materials and equipment weighing up to — and occasionally exceeding — 50 pounds, view a computer or other digital screen, work on a computer, workstation or comparable system, and make accurate entries in such systems. Manual dexterity and fine motor skills are required for detailed assembly and precision work. Work may take place in areas with varying temperatures or no climate control, varying noise levels, and production equipment in motion. Proper personal protective equipment (PPE) must be worn in designated areas at all times as required by company policy. Reasonable accommodations may be available to enable individuals with disabilities but are always subject to safety concerns for the employee and all team members. Any assessment will be performed by a third party vendor and will be reported on a pass/fail basis with no other medical information conveyed to employer.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Warehouse Operations
new_roles.description:
**Who We Are**

Stored Energy Systems (SENS) is an award-winning manufacturer of premium quality power conversion products located in Longmont, CO. In business for over 50 years, SENS is the market leader with a proven track record of providing highly reliable battery chargers, DC power systems, and related products to industrial markets. For more information on our company please see our web site at www.sens-usa.com.

**View the SENS Product Catalog**

**Summary**

The Senior Manager, Warehouse Operations leads the people, processes, and systems that maintain accurate inventory and reliable material flow across Stored Energy Systems (SENS) manufacturing operations. Based at Disc Drive headquarters, this role leads teams and team members across all SENS locations on first shift (days) and second shift (evenings). The role oversees receiving, warehousing, inventory control, material handling, production replenishment, kitting, inter-factory transportation, shipping, and freight coordination, while developing teams and operating capacity to support production continuity, customer deliveries, and growth.

**Responsibilities**

Leadership and Operating Performance

* Establish consistent material handling and inventory management standards, performance expectations, and accountability across all locations.
* Develop supervisors and team leaders through coaching, training, performance management, and succession planning.
* Own Warehouse Operations staffing plans and coordinate coverage, priorities, and escalation processes across all locations and both shifts to support production needs.
* Promote safe material handling and consistent workplace practices in partnership with the Environmental Health and Safety team.

Inventory Accuracy and Control

* Own inventory accuracy and control standards across SENS inventory locations, including inventory held at partner locations.
* Establish consistent receiving, put-away, picking, transfer, issue, return, and reconciliation processes in Infor SyteLine. Oversee receipt processing for non-inventory purchases.
* Lead cycle counting, inventory discrepancy investigations, root-cause analysis, and corrective actions.
* Maintain material identification, traceability, first-in, first-out practices, and segregation of restricted or nonconforming inventory.
* Partner with Procurement and Finance on inventory reconciliation and actions to improve inventory health, supporting Procurement’s ownership of inventory turns, safety stock levels, and excess and obsolete inventory.
* Lead preparation and execution of annual physical inventories at all SENS locations.

Production Material Flow

* Lead production material delivery, including stock picking, replenishment of point-of-use inventory areas, scheduled material delivery routes, and kanban replenishment parameters. Align execution with sales, inventory, and operations planning (SIOP) and production schedules.
* Develop and implement scalable assembly-phase kitting processes for configure-to-order and engineer-to-order products. Ensure kit accuracy, completeness, alignment with current revisions, staging, and return of unused materials.
* Coordinate material priorities, shortage escalations, and decisions about incomplete kits with Planning, Production, and Procurement.
* Establish visual management and kanban replenishment processes from kitting through delivery to production lines.

Transportation, Shipping, and Freight

* Own inter-factory transportation and inventory transfers, movement of finished products to shipping, and return flows for empty bins, carts, and protective packing materials.
* Lead local shipping operations and centralized inbound and outbound freight execution, coordinating with Planning & Fulfillment and Order Management to support on-time, complete customer shipments.
* Manage freight and premium freight costs against budget and maintain transportation contingency plans to support production continuity and customer deliveries.

Capacity and Continuous Improvement

* Translate production forecasts into logistics capacity plans. Lead warehouse and material-flow readiness for factory expansions and production ramps, including space, staffing, and training.
* Improve productivity through standard work, waste reduction, daily performance management, process automation, and enterprise resource planning (ERP) system improvements, in partnership with IT, Manufacturing Engineering, and Continuous Improvement.

**Required Qualifications**

* 8+ years of experience in manufacturing inventory, warehousing, and logistics, including 5+ years leading supervisors and teams across multiple sites and shifts.
* Demonstrated success scaling warehouse operations in a high-growth manufacturing environment.
* Strong knowledge of inventory controls, ERP transactions, cycle counting, kanban, supermarkets, production replenishment, and order kitting.
* Experience managing shipping operations, transportation providers, and freight costs.
* Experience supporting repetitive manufacturing production.
* Demonstrated ability to improve inventory accuracy, establish consistent operating practices, and develop effective supervisors and team leaders.
* Ability to analyze operational and financial data, resolve problems, and communicate priorities and issues across functions.
* Experience implementing Lean or continuous improvement initiatives.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, logistics, operations, engineering, or a related field
* Relevant supply chain, logistics, or Lean certification.
* Experience with Infor SyteLine, barcode scanning, and warehouse management systems.
* Experience in electrical equipment, industrial products, or similarly complex manufacturing environments.
* Experience supporting configure-to-order or engineer-to-order production.

**Location:** Longmont, CO

**Base Compensation:** $135,000 - $165,000 is the projected range of annual base salary for this role depending on the candidate’s overall qualifications and experience.

**Bonus:** This position is eligible for an annual bonus based on individual and company performance.

**Closing Date:** December 1st. While we expect to keep the position open through this date, the posting may be extended or closed early based on applicant volume and hiring needs.

**Onsite Perks**

* Free gym with 24/7 access
* Free Electric Vehicle charging
* Breakfast and Lunch Café
* After hours Grab & Go snacks
* Basketball court
* Walking paths

**Benefits**

* Paid Time Off
* Paid holidays
* Medical insurance
* Dental insurance
* Vision insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability
* Life insurance
* 401(k) plan with immediate vesting
* Employee referral program
* Tuition reimbursement
* Professional development

At SENS, our culture is rooted in a set of core values that reflect who we are and how we work. In a recent 2025 poll, our employees identified the values that best define us: *“Innovative”, “Respectful”, “Inviting”, “Flexible”, “Collaborative”, and “Growth Driven”.* Our team describes us as a dynamic, forward-thinking company where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

We pride ourselves on being an equal opportunity employer, fully dedicated to fostering inclusion and diversity. We welcome all applicants, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

We hope you're interested in making a difference with us. Even if you don't feel that you meet every qualification listed in this job description, we still encourage you to apply.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Quality Engineering
new_roles.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Manager, Quality Engineering is a senior leader responsible for leading complex, high-profile quality engineering initiatives across multiple applications, platforms, delivery teams, and implementation timelines, including solutions provided or supported by external vendors. This role provides program-level leadership, technical direction, coordination, and influence across cross-functional teams to ensure quality is built into every phase of the software delivery lifecycle.

The position develops and drives comprehensive quality strategies for strategic initiatives, including integrated test planning, risk-based testing, end-to-end validation, automation adoption, defect prevention, release readiness, and production quality. The role partners with Product, Engineering, Business Analysis, Architecture, Production Support, Delivery, business stakeholders, and vendor teams to align dependencies, resolve risks, and deliver measurable quality outcomes.

The role also supports the Aetna Medicare Technology Quality Engineering Program Management Office by helping manage the QE initiative portfolio, establishing consistent governance and reporting practices, monitoring milestones and dependencies, and providing leadership visibility into quality risks, delivery health, resource constraints, and release confidence.

Key Responsibilities

* Lead end-to-end quality engineering planning and execution for complex initiatives spanning multiple applications, platforms, releases, delivery teams, and vendors.
* Develop integrated, risk-based QE strategies covering scope, test levels, environments, data, automation, dependencies, quality gates, and release-readiness criteria.
* Coordinate functional, integration, end-to-end, regression, performance, operational-readiness, and production-validation testing across internal and vendor teams.
* Maintain a holistic view of milestones, dependencies, risks, defects, resource constraints, vendor commitments, and delivery readiness; drive mitigation and escalation as needed.
* Establish quality expectations, deliverables, evidence requirements, acceptance criteria, and accountability measures for vendor partners and third-party solutions.
* Lead the AMT QE Program Management Office with initiative intake, prioritization, portfolio roadmaps, governance, dependency management, metrics, and executive reporting.
* Facilitate cross-functional governance, planning, status, defect, risk, and readiness forums to align stakeholders, resolve barriers, and drive timely decisions.
* Promote early quality engagement, root-cause analysis, defect prevention, and continuous improvement across the software delivery lifecycle.
* Advance test automation and AI-enabled QE capabilities to improve coverage, efficiency, maintainability, defect analysis, and quality insights.
* Define and communicate quality, vendor, release-confidence, and production-readiness metrics, using actionable insights to improve stability, delivery predictability, and business outcomes.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field—or equivalent practical experience—and eight or more years of experience in quality assurance, quality engineering, testing, software delivery, or technical program delivery.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex QE initiatives across multiple applications, platforms, teams, vendors, and delivery timelines while influencing outcomes without direct reporting authority.
* Proven ability to develop integrated, risk-based test strategies spanning functional, integration, end-to-end, regression, automation, and production-readiness testing.
* Experience with Agile or hybrid delivery, quality governance, defect and release management, risk and dependency management, quality transformation, and executive-level metrics and reporting.
* Strong analytical, facilitation, organizational, communication, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, navigate ambiguity, resolve cross-team barriers, and drive work to completion.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience supporting healthcare, insurance, claims processing, enrollment, payment, or Medicare platforms.
* Experience with large-scale implementations involving multiple internal applications and external vendor solutions.
* Experience supporting a Quality Engineering Program Management Office, testing center of excellence, portfolio governance function, or enterprise transformation program.
* Experience with automation frameworks and AI-assisted quality engineering.
* Knowledge of observability, monitoring, performance testing, production validation, and operational-readiness practices.
* Experience defining quality scorecards, release-confidence measures, vendor performance indicators, or QE maturity models.

**Education**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field—or equivalent practical experience—and eight or more years of experience in quality assurance, quality engineering, testing, software delivery, or technical program delivery.

The typical pay range for this role is:

$106,605.00 - $260,590.00

This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. This position is eligible for a CVS Health bonus, commission or short-term incentive program in addition to the base pay range listed above. This position also includes an award target in the company’s equity award program.

new_roles.description:
»

**Date:** Nov 12, 2026

**Location:** North Reading, MA, US

**Company:** Teradyne

We are the global test and automation specialists, powering next-generation technologies through sophisticated solutions. Behind every electronic device you use, Teradyne's test technology ensures your device works right the first time, every time! Our portfolio of automation solutions help manufacturers to develop and deliver products quickly, efficiently and cost-effectively. Together, Teradyne companies deliver manufacturing automation across industries and applications around the world!

 

We attract, develop, and retain a high-performance workforce, comprised of people with diverse backgrounds and a shared drive for excellence. We strive to foster a positive and inclusive work environment that helps employees, and communities, thrive.

**Our Purpose**

TERADYNE, where experience meets innovation and driving excellence in every connection. We are fueled by creativity and diversity of thought and in our workforce. Our employees are supported to innovate and learn something new every day.

We cultivate a culture of inclusion for all employees that respects their individual strengths, views, and experiences. We believe that our differences enable us to be a better team – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better business results.

 

**Opportunity Overview**

The Senior Director, Product Quality & Customer Excellence owns customer-perceived quality for Teradyne’s Compute Test Division, from design through the field. Reporting to the division’s VP of Engineering, this high-visibility role leads Software Quality Engineering and drives quality across hardware, software, FPGA, ASIC, applications, manufacturing, and service engineering. You will work with our executive team and largest customers to build the quality organization and reputation of the division.

* Lead customer escalations from first call to closure, driving Severity 1 and 2 escalations down 20 to 30% every year.
* Develop design reviews, risk analysis, and release gates that engineering respects and that stop a bad release.
* Collaborate with engineering leaders across organizations you do not manage, earning their commitment through credibility, data, and follow-through.
* Build trusted relationships with top customers, and cut field defect escapes every year while shipping every major launch clean through its first six months.
* Partner with leadership to show the cost of poor quality and the margin benefit of reducing it, and close more than 95% of corrective actions on time.
* Mentor and retain exceptional quality engineers, and develop the next generation of quality leaders.
 

**All About You**

We seek individuals who share our passion and determination. Our commitment to customer success drives us to go the extra mile. If you’re ready to join us in this mission, take a closer look at the minimum criteria for the position.

* BS in Software Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience (MS a plus)
* Typically 15+ years in quality, engineering, product development, or applications, including 10+ years leading cross-functional teams on complex technical products
* A measured, visible quality turnaround or product launch you can point to
* Strong command of product development, verification and validation, reliability, and field operations
* Proven success building and leading teams, including managers
* Direct experience working with executive-level customers
* Ability to take a big, ambiguous, high-stakes problem and drive it to done without waiting to be pushed
* Accountability for outcomes, not activity: you set targets publicly, then hit them or own the miss, and you tell the truth early
* A customer-first mindset, leading and influencing across organizations by earning commitment
* Preferred: experience in semiconductor test equipment (ATE), test and measurement, capital equipment, networking, or enterprise infrastructure
* Preferred: product quality leadership in mission critical, complex hardware and software systems
* Preferred: a track record of using AI, automation, and data to measurably speed up root-cause analysis and problem closure
 

If this role excites you but your background does not match every bullet above, we would still love to hear from you.

 

*We are only considering candidates local to position location and are unable to provide relocation for this position.*

*This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.*

 

**Compensation:**
 
The base salary range for this role is $228,200 - $365,100. This range is a good faith estimate, and the amount of base salary will correspond with experience and skill set. This range can also fluctuate depending on demand and location.

**Incentive Plan:** This job is eligible for discretionary bonus(es) based on financial performance.

 

**Benefits:**
 
Teradyne offers a variety of robust health and well-being benefit programs, including medical, dental, vision, Flexible Spending Accounts, retirement savings plans, life and disability insurance, paid vacation & holidays, tuition assistance programs, and more.

new_roles.title: SR. Manager, Automation and Controls (Manufacturing Plant)
new_roles.description:
**Job Description Summary:**

At The Coca-Cola Company, we bring together the power of our people, our brands, technology and innovation to refresh the world and make a difference. Our manufacturing operations are critical to delivering quality products safely, efficiently and reliably, and automation plays an increasingly important role in how we build the manufacturing environment of the future.

 

The **Senior Manager, Automation and Controls** will be based at our Ontario, California facility and will lead automation and controls capabilities that support safe, reliable and efficient manufacturing operations. This role will have primary responsibility for the Ontario facility while providing limited automation and controls support to our Portland facility, requiring approximately 5% travel.

This position will lead a small team of Automation and Controls Technicians and serve as a senior technical resource for automation, controls, instrumentation and manufacturing systems. The role will partner closely with Engineering, Maintenance, Operations, Quality, Safety and Information Technology teams to improve equipment reliability, strengthen controls infrastructure, support capital projects and advance manufacturing technology.

The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise in industrial automation and controls with practical manufacturing experience, strong problem-solving capabilities and effective people leadership. They bring a continuous-improvement mindset and can translate operational challenges into sustainable automation solutions while developing the technical capabilities of their team.

 

**Key Responsibilities and Position-Related Functions**
-------------------------------------------------------

* Lead and develop a small team of Automation and Controls Technicians, establishing clear priorities, technical standards, development plans and expectations for safe and effective execution.
* Provide technical leadership for the Ontario manufacturing facility across industrial automation, programmable logic controllers (Rockwell PLC Platform), human-machine interfaces, supervisory control systems, instrumentation, industrial networks, motion control and related manufacturing technologies.
* Ignition Software Platform and Database Development experience.
* Provide limited automation and controls support for the Portland facility, including technical troubleshooting, project consultation and alignment on controls standards, with approximately 5% travel.
* Partner with Operations, Maintenance and Engineering teams to identify chronic equipment issues, determine root causes and implement controls and automation solutions that improve reliability, throughput and operating performance.
* Lead troubleshooting of complex controls and automation issues, using structured problem-solving, equipment data and technical expertise to reduce downtime and prevent recurrence.
* Establish and maintain controls standards, system documentation, software backups, change-management practices and lifecycle strategies for automation assets.
* Support capital projects from concept through commissioning by developing technical requirements, evaluating automation solutions, reviewing control system designs and ensuring successful installation, testing, start-up and handover.
* Partner with internal teams, original equipment manufacturers, system integrators and other technical suppliers to ensure automation solutions meet operational requirements and established Coca-Cola standards.
* Develop strategies for managing aging or obsolete controls hardware and software, prioritizing replacements based on operational risk, equipment criticality and business needs.
* Strengthen preventive and predictive maintenance practices for automation and controls systems to improve equipment availability and reduce unplanned failures.
* Use manufacturing and controls data to identify performance trends, recurring losses and improvement opportunities, translating data into actionable recommendations.
* Advance digital manufacturing capabilities by evaluating appropriate applications of connected systems, advanced analytics and artificial intelligence-enabled tools to improve troubleshooting, reliability and decision-making.
* Collaborate with Information Technology and appropriate cybersecurity partners to help protect industrial control environments, maintain appropriate system access and support secure industrial network architecture.
* Ensure automation work supports applicable safety, quality, environmental and regulatory requirements, including safe equipment design and control of hazardous energy.
* Drive continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to simplify systems, improve equipment performance, reduce waste and energy consumption, and increase the long-term reliability and maintainability of manufacturing assets.
Build technical capability across the organization through coaching, documentation, standardized troubleshooting practices and knowledge sharing with technicians, maintenance teams and other manufacturing partners. 

**Education and Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Automation Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Engineering or a related technical discipline.
* 8+ years of progressive experience in industrial automation, controls engineering, electrical systems or manufacturing engineering, preferably within a high-speed manufacturing, food and beverage, consumer packaged goods or similarly complex production environment.
* Demonstrated experience leading, supervising or developing automation, controls or technical professionals in a manufacturing environment.
* Strong hands-on knowledge of programmable logic controller programming, human-machine interfaces, industrial controls, instrumentation, variable-frequency drives, servo or motion systems and industrial communication networks.
* Experience troubleshooting complex automated equipment and applying structured root-cause analysis to recurring equipment and controls failures.
* Experience supporting manufacturing capital projects, including controls specifications, design review, system integration, factory or site acceptance testing, commissioning and start-up.
* Working knowledge of industrial control system cybersecurity principles, network segmentation, access management, backup and recovery practices, and disciplined automation change management.
* Strong data literacy with the ability to use manufacturing information, equipment data and digital tools to identify trends, diagnose performance issues and prioritize improvement opportunities.
* Demonstrated digital fluency and an understanding of how advanced analytics and artificial intelligence tools can responsibly support manufacturing reliability, troubleshooting, predictive maintenance and operational decision-making.
* Knowledge of electrical and machine safety practices and applicable industrial standards, with the ability to integrate safety requirements into automation and controls solutions.
* Demonstrated ability to manage competing technical priorities, respond effectively to critical manufacturing issues and balance immediate production needs with sustainable long-term solutions.
* Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to explain complex technical issues to technical and non-technical partners and influence decisions across Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Quality, Safety and Information Technology.
