**Knowledge and Skills:**

• Broad expertise in **Device and Combination Product Quality Assurance, QMS, and operational Quality oversight** .

• Strong knowledge of **ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 14971** , and applicable global regulatory requirements.

• Demonstrated experience with **CDMO/external partner oversight, supplier Quality, testing, audits, and inspection readiness** .

• Strong understanding of **design controls, design transfer, risk management, manufacturing controls, supplier controls, and product realization** .

• Proven experience with **CAPA, investigations, deviations, change control, complaints, and quality risk management** .

• Demonstrated capability to serve as **Management Representative** , including QMS performance, management review, compliance oversight, and risk escalation.

• Strong **strategic thinking, business acumen, risk-based decision-making, and problem-solving** skills.

• Ability to influence senior leaders and drive outcomes in a **complex, matrixed organization** .

**About The Role:**

As a CBRE VAS Quality & Risk Management (QRM) Senior Director, identifies, manages and mitigates risk through an established global framework leveraging our perspectives, scale and connections to provide industry-leading valuation and advisory services. Institutional Funds Valuations (IVAS) is a fast growing department of CBRE VAS Dedicated to servicing the appraisal requirements of large institutional fund clients. The purpose of this position is to implement the CBRE Quality and Risk Management (QRM) function within IVAS.

This will include the enforcement, oversight and delivery of the QRM Framework as applicable to IVAS.

You will engage with clients and will be an integral part of both the IVAS department and the QRM team, with a passion for innovation and the desire to build something unique.

**What You'll Do:**

* The QRM Director (IVAS) is an experienced appraisal professional who serves as the subject matter expert for the implementation and delivery of the QRM Framework across IVAS.
* The role is key to ensuring processes, procedures and the delivery of services are in line with regulatory, client and internal guidelines while also providing ongoing support for appraisers and IVAS management to manage risk.
* The QRM Director (IVAS) will predominantly provide approval of incoming Risk Assessments (RA) and participate in the appraisal review process, ensuring all appraisals are of high quality, comply with internal guidelines, uphold appraiser independence and are in line with regulatory and client standards, including USPAP requirements.
* The QRM Director (IVAS) will collaborate closely with all key stakeholders to drive Quality and Risk Management initiatives within the Division and align these initiatives with both the United States and Global QRM Business Plan.
* Responsibilities include ensuring compliance, as applicable, with the Global and United States QRM Framework through the following activities:
* Ensuring IVAS compliance with the CBRE VAS Appraisal Report Review Process, including personally completing reviews within the IVAS line of business within agreed turnaround time requirements.
* Ensuring IVAS adherence to VAS Practice Area Guidelines (PAG) and key risk mitigation procedures.
* Following Risk Assessment procedures.
* Following escalation procedures.
* Implementing systems to track client contracting status.
* Following and implementing audit procedures.
* In conjunction with Senior QRM Management, driving and delivering initiatives to embed Core-QRM Operational Concepts into IVAS Workflow Platforms.
* Identifying knowledge needs, assisting with best-practice communications, training, continuing education and mentoring as directed by QRM Senior Management.
* Gathering client feedback, identifying process gaps and improvement opportunities, and supporting technology innovation.
* Creating and maintaining all registers/licenses and associated procedures to ensure regulatory, client, QRM Framework and PAG requirements are met.
* Unless otherwise advised, ensuring all master service agreements and valuation and advisory contracts are executed in accordance with QRM Framework and PAG requirements.
* Supporting business development initiatives by participating in proposal responses and new business initiatives, and preparing marketing material/pitches, with a particular focus on communicating the benefits of QRM.
* Improving CBRE’s position during contractual negotiations by actively participating in strategy planning and client meetings, with a particular focus on capping of liability.

* Bachelor's Degree with a minimum of 10 years of commercial appraisal experience, preferably involved with Institutional Funds clients. * Experience in the areas of staffing, selection, training, development, coaching, mentoring, measuring, appraising, and rewarding performance and retention is preferred.
* Advanced knowledge of the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP) preferred.
* Ability to lead the exchange of complicated and difficult information, convey performance expectations, and handle problems.
* Leadership skills to set, manage, and achieve targets with a direct impact on multiple department results within a function.

* Expert organizational skills and an advanced inquisitive approach.

When you join CBRE, you become part of the global leader in commercial real estate services and investment that helps businesses and people thrive. We are dynamic problem solvers and forward-thinking professionals who create significant impact. Our collaborative culture is built on our shared values — respect, integrity, service and excellence — and we value the diverse perspectives, backgrounds and skillsets of our people. At CBRE, you have the opportunity to chart your own course and realize your potential. We welcome all applicants.

**Our Values in Hiring**

At CBRE, we are committed to fostering a culture where everyone feels they belong. We value diverse perspectives and experiences, and we welcome all applications.

At Ecore, we transform reclaimed rubber into innovative performance surfaces that protect people and the planet. Our products power everything from playgrounds and gyms to hospitals, courts, and even rockets—helping people in motion be their strongest, healthiest selves. As a high-growth, sustainability-driven company, we’re leading the way in circular innovation by keeping rubber out of landfills and turning waste into wellness, safety, and performance. We’re excited to find individuals who are eager to be part of a team that’s driving global impact through innovation, sustainability, and purpose.
  
  
**Location:** 715 Fountain Avenue, Lancaster, PA 17601
  
  
Lead a High-Performing Manufacturing Operation and Drive Operational Excellence
  
Are you a hands-on manufacturing leader who thrives on building strong teams, improving performance, and creating a culture of accountability and continuous improvement? We are seeking a Plant Manager to lead all aspects of site operations, including safety, quality, delivery, cost, maintenance, and employee development.
  
This is an opportunity to make a lasting impact in a close-knit manufacturing environment where leadership matters, employee engagement is valued, and continuous improvement is part of the culture. We're looking for a servant leader who is willing to roll up their sleeves, develop people, challenge the status quo, and drive measurable business results.
  
What You'll Do
  
As Plant Manager, you will have full responsibility for the performance of the facility and will lead efforts to achieve world-class results in:
  

* Safety performance and employee engagement
* Product quality and customer satisfaction
* On-time delivery and schedule attainment
* Cost control and operational efficiency
* Maintenance and facility reliability
* Continuous improvement and Lean manufacturing initiatives

You will lead a team of supervisors and managers while partnering closely with Planning, Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, Customer Service, and Finance to ensure the site consistently meets customer expectations and business objectives.
  
Key Responsibilities
  

* Lead daily plant operations to ensure safety, quality, delivery, and cost targets are achieved.
* Develop, coach, and mentor supervisors and department leaders.
* Foster a culture built on accountability, trust, teamwork, and servant leadership.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives utilizing Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 6S, and other operational excellence tools.
* Monitor and improve key performance metrics, including Quality, Delivery, and Cost (QDC).
* Oversee production scheduling, capacity planning, labor utilization, and inventory management.
* Ensure maintenance programs support operational reliability and uptime.
* Manage plant budgets, capital projects, labor expenses, and maintenance costs.
* Conduct regular Gemba walks, safety reviews, audits, and performance discussions.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental regulations, and company safety standards.
* Partner with Supply Chain and Planning teams to support customer demand and on-time delivery goals.

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Operations Management, or a related field, or equivalent manufacturing leadership experience.
* 10+ years of manufacturing leadership experience.
* Minimum 5 years of experience as a Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or comparable site leader.
* Proven success leading salaried supervisors and managers in a multi-shift manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated track record of improving safety, quality, delivery, and cost metrics.
* Experience working with ERP/MRP systems for production scheduling, inventory, and shop floor operations.
* Strong financial acumen with experience managing labor, maintenance, and capital budgets.
* Knowledge of production scheduling, capacity planning, and manufacturing operations.
* Working knowledge of OSHA and environmental compliance requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience leading operational turnarounds or transformational change initiatives.
* Background in manufacturing environments involving assembly, metal fabrication, sheet metal, packaging, mechanical components, fasteners, or related industrial products.

* A servant leader who develops people and builds strong teams.
* A culture builder capable of leading organizational change.
* A proactive problem solver who challenges convention and drives improvement.
* A leader who creates accountability rather than simply managing tasks.
* Equally comfortable on the production floor and in strategic planning discussions.

Why Join Us?
  

* Opportunity to lead a highly visible manufacturing operation.
* Strong support from executive leadership.
* Collaborative, team-oriented culture.
* Ability to drive operational improvements and leave a lasting impact.
* Opportunity to develop employees, strengthen culture, and improve business performance.

If you have a passion for manufacturing leadership, continuous improvement, and developing high-performing teams, we encourage you to apply. Your leadership can help shape the future of our operation while making a meaningful impact on our employees, customers, and community.
  
Apply today and become the leader who drives the next chapter of operational excellence.

**Role Summary**

Parklane is opening a brand-new manufacturing facility in Michigan, and we are looking for a Plant Manager to work with us to build it from the ground up. As the senior leader on site, you will have accountability for the plant: safety, quality, delivery, cost, people, and culture. You will lead a team of up to 150 employees and be supported by Parklane’s shared services groups, including Engineering, Supply Chain, Human Resources, and Finance, so you can focus on running a safe, high-performing operation and setting the standard for how Parklane operates in Michigan.

**Key Responsibilities**

Site Leadership & Start-Up

* Own the overall performance of the Michigan facility, including safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, and cost
* Lead the ramp-up of the new site, establishing operating rhythms, processes, and standards aligned with Parklane’s practices
* Develop and execute site plans and budgets in partnership with Finance and senior leadership
* Serve as the face of Parklane in the local community, with customers, vendors, and regulators

Operations & Production

* Direct day-to-day manufacturing, fabrication, assembly, and shipping activities to meet customer commitments
* Work with production scheduling and Supply Chain to balance capacity, labor, and material availability
* Drive continuous improvement and lean practices to improve throughput, reduce waste, and control cost
* Track and report on site KPIs, and act quickly on gaps to plan

Safety, Quality & Compliance

* Champion a safety-first culture and ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, and applicable federal, state, and local requirements
* Partner with QHSE to implement and sustain Parklane’s quality management system and drive corrective actions to closure
* Maintain a clean, organized, audit-ready facility and well-maintained equipment

People Leadership

* Recruit, develop, and lead plant leaders, supervisors, and front-line teams, building a strong bench for a growing site
* Partner with Human Resources on hiring, onboarding, employee relations, performance management, and engagement
* Set clear expectations, coach for accountability, and recognize results in line with Parklane’s core values
* Build a positive, inclusive culture where employees feel safe, respected, and invested in the site’s success

Cross-Functional Collaboration

* Work closely with Engineering on product design, manufacturability, and technical issues
* Partner with Supply Chain on procurement, inventory, logistics, and supplier performance
* Collaborate with Finance on budgeting, cost control, and financial reporting
* Leverage shared services across the organization to support the site efficiently, and provide feedback to continuously improve that support

**Qualifications and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
* 8+ years of progressive manufacturing operations experience, including 3+ years in a plant management or senior site leadership role
* Proven experience leading a workforce of 100+ in a manufacturing or fabrication environment
* Experience launching, expanding, or transforming a facility is a strong asset
* Strong working knowledge of lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, and quality systems (ISO 9001 exposure preferred)
* Solid understanding of OSHA and workplace safety, environmental, and employment regulations in the U.S.
* Financial acumen, including budgeting, P&L awareness, and cost management
* Experience with ERP systems and data-driven performance management (D365 an asset)
* Strong leadership, communication, and decision-making skills, with the ability to influence across a matrixed organization
* Hands-on, accountable, and comfortable building structure in a fast-paced, evolving environment

**About Parklane**

As one of North America’s leading providers of turnkey mechanical noise control and VIRS solutions, Parklane is on a constant search for top industry talent. Every day we help clients with their sound attenuation and vibration challenges. We do it by leveraging an agile approach to engineering, product manufacturing and implementation.

As an organization, we live and breathe our core values:

1. Challenge Accepted

2. Work Hard & Play Hard

3. Share the Wins & Own the Losses, and

4. Build Together, Grow Together

By sharing ideas and supporting each other at every turn, we’ve built a reputation both for service excellence and the strength of our workplace culture. Put simply, our team is committed to doing whatever it takes to help our customers succeed—and that’s why we need professionals with the experience and expertise to solve complex problems.

Pay: $125,000.00 - $150,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

protected_roles.description:
At Radius Packaging, our relentless focus on innovation and operational excellence is just one of the reasons our customers enjoy working with us. Our unique company culture, progressive leadership, and dedicated members mean that who we are is just as important as what we do.

For fifty years, we've had fun supplying plastic packaging for diverse consumer and commercial markets. Our members take pride in creating and delivering products they care about, going the extra mile to help our customers and our business succeed. From containers for food, beverage, and personal care products to household and industrial chemicals, Radius Packaging continues to enhance our capabilities as a full-scope packaging provider. Based in New Berlin, Wisconsin, with a second facility in Delavan, we have approximately 260 members.

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated **Plant Manager** to lead our New Berlin manufacturing facility. Reporting to the Director of Manufacturing, this leader is responsible for the overall performance of the facility across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, People Development, Maintenance, and Continuous Improvement, with accountability for plant P&L performance and operational execution.

We're looking for more than someone who can manage today's production. We want a leader who thinks ahead, prevents problems before they occur, builds strong systems and processes, and ensures improvements are sustained.

The ideal candidate brings a strong engineering and systems-thinking mindset, understands the financial drivers of manufacturing performance, communicates effectively at all levels, and knows how to create accountability while developing and recognizing a high-performing team.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

### **Lead Plant Performance**

* Provide overall leadership for plant operations, including safety, quality, production, maintenance, delivery, cost, food safety, and continuous improvement.
* Establish and manage key performance indicators for safety, quality, delivery, OEE, labor productivity, cost, equipment reliability, and member engagement.
* Maintain a visible, practical, hands-on leadership presence throughout the facility.
* Bring urgency to plant and equipment performance while proactively addressing risks that could affect safety, quality, delivery, cost, or customer commitments.

### **Build Systems That Prevent Problems**

* Build, implement, and sustain prevention-focused systems and processes that improve operational consistency, equipment reliability, product quality, and financial performance.
* Use strong engineering and systems thinking to assess performance and solve complex operational challenges.
* Lead structured root-cause analysis and ensure corrective and preventive actions are implemented, verified for effectiveness, and sustained.
* Partner with plant leadership to strengthen predictive and preventive maintenance strategies that reduce unplanned downtime and improve equipment reliability.

### **Own Financial & Operational Results**

* Own plant P&L performance, including budgeting, forecasting, cost control, labor utilization, operating expenses, maintenance spending, and capital investment planning.
* Direct plant activities and coordinate priorities across functions to achieve manufacturing and customer objectives in a timely and cost-effective manner.
* Manage facilities, capital assets, and equipment utilization while identifying opportunities for repair, replacement, automation, and capital improvement.

### **Drive Accountability & Continuous Improvement**

* Create disciplined action plans with clear owners, due dates, review processes, and escalation through completion.
* Lead Lean, continuous improvement, and 6S efforts and ensure improvements are incorporated into standard work and sustained over time.
* Promote accountability while recognizing individuals and teams who meet commitments, improve performance, and demonstrate strong ownership.

### **Develop Great People**

* Build, lead, and develop a capable, engaged, and high-performing team.
* Lead effective hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, succession planning, and recognition.
* Create alignment across departments and organizational levels through clear, proactive communication.
* Support cross-functional priorities and build strong partnerships throughout the organization.

### **Champion Safety, Quality & Compliance**

* Ensure compliance with established safety, health, quality, GMP, food safety, food quality, Company policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
* Foster an environment where safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement are part of how work gets done every day.

**What You'll Bring**
---------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Manufacturing, Business, or a related field.
* At least 8 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including responsibility for plant operations or multiple operational functions.
* Proven experience leading managers, supervisors, and cross-functional teams in a manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated P&L accountability, including budgeting, forecasting, cost control, capital planning, and financial performance management.
* Strong engineering, technical, and systems-thinking capabilities with demonstrated success identifying, solving, and preventing operational issues.
* Experience leading root-cause analysis and implementing sustainable corrective and preventive actions.
* Demonstrated ability to establish and manage operational metrics, action plans, ownership, due dates, and follow-through to completion.
* Proven ability to build, develop, engage, and retain high-performing teams.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to create alignment across all levels of an organization.
* Experience applying Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, TPM, Six Sigma, or comparable operational excellence methodologies.

**The Leader Who Will Thrive Here**
-----------------------------------

You are a leader who doesn't simply react to today's problems. You build systems that prevent tomorrow's.

You combine an engineering mindset with strong business judgment and understand the connection between people, process, equipment reliability, operational metrics, and financial performance. You establish clear expectations, create ownership, follow through on commitments, recognize strong performance, and make sure improvements stick.

Most importantly, you're comfortable being where the work happens. You can move effectively between reviewing plant financial performance, coaching a leader, solving an operational problem, reviewing equipment reliability, and walking the manufacturing floor with the team.

If you are energized by building strong teams, strengthening manufacturing systems, solving complex problems, and creating sustainable operational results, we'd love to hear from you.

**Preparedness today, safer tomorrow.**

Emergent is a leading public health company that delivers protective and life-saving solutions to
  
communities around the world.

We go where others won’t, taking on some of the biggest public health challenges to protect and enhance millions of lives, and create a better, more secure world. Here, you will join passionate professionals who advance their scientific, technical and professional skills to develop products designed to protect and enhance life.

  

**Why This Role Matters**

At Emergent, our work protects communities and strengthens global health security. As **Head of IT Infrastructure & Operations**, you will lead the organization’s global technology infrastructure and end-user services.

Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Senior Director, Head of IT Infrastructure & Operations leads the strategy, engineering, security, reliability, and day-to-day operation of the company’s global technology infrastructure and end-user services. The role is accountable for resilient, secure, compliant, and cost-effective delivery across hybrid cloud, data centers, networks, compute, storage, workplace technology, service management, collaboration, and infrastructure platforms supporting a global 24/7 business and regulated operations. The position modernizes the infrastructure operating model through automation, observability, data-driven service management, and responsible use of AI, while maintaining disciplined lifecycle, continuity, validation, and vendor governance.

  

**What You'll Do**

*Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.*

**Enterprise leadership and strategy**

* Serve as a member of the CIO’s IT Leadership Team and act as the executive owner for enterprise infrastructure and operations capabilities.
* Define and execute a multi-year infrastructure and operations strategy, architecture, investment roadmap, lifecycle plan, and operating model aligned to business priorities, enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, data strategy, and application modernization.
* Translate technology choices into clear business outcomes, risks, service commitments, investment requirements, and decision points for senior leaders.
* Bring an infrastructure, integration, resiliency, and operability perspective to enterprise programs, acquisitions, site changes, and major technology initiatives.

**Hybrid cloud, platforms, and architecture**

* Lead a fit-for-purpose hybrid cloud strategy spanning public cloud, SaaS, private hosting, and on-premises environments; establish standards for landing zones, connectivity, identity integration, workload placement, scalability, portability, and cost governance.
* Own infrastructure architecture and engineering standards for networks, compute, storage, backup, recovery, databases and middleware where assigned, collaboration, telephony, endpoint and workplace platforms, and core operational tooling.
* Partner with application, data, security, quality, and business teams to ensure platforms are interoperable, supportable, validated where required, and designed for availability, performance, recoverability, and lifecycle sustainability.
* Establish technology currency and technical-debt practices that reduce unsupported platforms, single points of failure, and avoid operational risk.

**Operational excellence, service management, and employee experience**

* Lead global 24/7 infrastructure operations, service desk, workplace services, major incident management, problem management, change enablement, configuration and asset practices, capacity management, and service continuity.
* Establish service catalogs, service ownership, service level objectives and agreements, operational level agreements, KPIs, experience measures, and executive reporting that connect service performance to business impact.
* Build mature monitoring, observability, event management, and command-center practices to identify degradation early, accelerate restoration, and drive permanent corrective action.
* Continuously improve employee technology experience across offices, laboratories, manufacturing and distribution environments, remote work, and executive support.

**Cyber resilience, continuity, and compliance**

* Partner with the Chief Information Security Officer and Quality organization to embed secure-by-design, zero-trust, privileged-access, vulnerability, patching, hardening, segmentation, backup protection, recovery, and logging requirements into infrastructure services.
* Own infrastructure disaster recovery and technology continuity capabilities, including business-aligned recovery objectives, dependency mapping, crisis response integration, documented recovery procedures, and regular exercises.
* Ensure infrastructure services meet applicable company policies and regulated-life-sciences requirements, including controlled change, documentation, qualification or validation, data integrity, audit readiness, and evidence retention where required.
* Ensure operational risks, exceptions, and control gaps are visible, assigned, prioritized, and remediated or formally accepted.

**Automation, AI-enabled operations, and data**

* Develop an automation-first operating model using infrastructure as code, orchestration, self-service, policy as code, automated testing, and repeatable deployment and recovery patterns.
* Adopt AI-enabled operations responsibly to improve event correlation, knowledge retrieval, service desk support, capacity forecasting, anomaly detection, and operational decision support, with appropriate human oversight, security, privacy, records, and compliance controls.
* Create trusted operational data and dashboards that enable trend analysis, predictive insight, cost transparency, risk prioritization, and measurable continual improvement.
* Build workforce capability in cloud, automation, AI, cybersecurity, service reliability, and modern engineering practices.

**Financial, supplier, and talent leadership**

* Own infrastructure and operations financial planning, forecasting, cloud financial management, contract optimization, and investment prioritization.
* Lead strategic sourcing activities, including RFPs, RFIs, SOWs, contract and service-level negotiations, supplier performance, concentration risk, exit planning, and third-party resilience.
* Lead, develop, and retain a diverse global team; clarify accountabilities, succession, cross-training, on-call expectations, and skills plans across employees, managed service providers, and specialist partners.
* Create a culture of ownership, disciplined execution, transparency, collaboration, learning, and continuous improvement.
  

The above statements describe the general nature of work performed in this job. They are not an exhaustive list of duties, and other duties may be assigned.

  

**What You Bring**

  

* Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, business, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. Advanced degree is preferred.
* Typically 15+ years of progressive technology experience, including 7+ years leading multiple infrastructure, operations, engineering, or service delivery teams in a complex global enterprise.
* Demonstrated success leading enterprise-wide infrastructure transformation and operating-model change in a highly regulated environment; life-sciences, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or manufacturing experience is strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated accountability for global, business-critical, 24/7 services delivered through a mix of internal teams, public cloud, SaaS, IaaS, PaaS, colocation, telecommunications, managed services, and outsourcing partners.

**Required Skills and Abilities**

* Executive leadership, business acumen, financial stewardship, and the ability to communicate complex technology choices as business value, risk, resilience, cost, and employee impact.
* Deep working knowledge of hybrid cloud, enterprise networking, compute, storage, backup and recovery, identity dependencies, endpoint and workplace technology, collaboration, telephony, monitoring, observability, and service management.
* Experience with modern engineering and operations practices, including automation, infrastructure as code, configuration management, APIs, DevSecOps, site reliability concepts, capacity engineering, and technology lifecycle management.
* Ability to establish metrics and use operational, experience, risk, and financial data to prioritize work and demonstrate outcomes.
* Strong knowledge of cybersecurity infrastructure controls and close partnership with security teams on zero trust, segmentation, vulnerability and patch management, privileged access, secure configuration, logging, resilience, and incident response.
* Experience designing, testing, and improving business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities across complex application and infrastructure dependencies.
* Knowledge of cGMP expectations and experience supporting validated or qualified technology in regulated life-sciences environments, including change control, documentation, data integrity, and audit readiness.
* Experience governing AI-enabled operational use cases with appropriate controls for security, privacy, compliance, transparency, reliability, and human oversight.
* Proven ability to lead in a matrixed environment, build coalitions, influence executives, negotiate with suppliers, and manage competing priorities during incidents and transformation.
* Strong talent leadership, coaching, succession planning, organizational design, sourcing strategy, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

protected_roles.description:
**NOTICE: The posting for local applicants only - is not for those applying for a global assignment and/or for employees working outside of Cipla's U.S. Subsidiaries or Affiliates.**

  

**Job Title**: Senior. Manager, Quality Control

**FLSA Classification**: Full-Time, Exempt Professional

**Work Location**: Central Islip, NY (Unit 3)

**Work Hours:** General Shift: 8:30AM – 5:00PM (may vary based on business needs)

**Reports To**: Quality Control Director

**Salary: $103,000 - $136,000**

  

**Position Summary**

The Manager, Finished Product & Stability Quality Control is responsible for leading all analytical testing, stability program execution, laboratory compliance activities, investigations, and personnel management associated with Finished Product and Stability testing. The role ensures compliance with cGMP, FDA, ICH, USP, Data Integrity, and internal quality requirements while supporting product release, stability commitments, regulatory inspections, and continuous improvement initiatives.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Manage Finished Product and Stability testing activities to support commercial product release and ongoing stability programs.
* Oversee testing and review of assay, related substances, chromatographic purity, degradation products, dissolution, content uniformity, residual solvents, and other compendial requirements.
* Ensure timely execution of stability sample pulls, testing, data review, trending, and reporting activities.
* Lead laboratory investigations including OOS, OOT, deviations, atypical results, and CAPA implementation.
* Review and approve analytical data, laboratory records, chromatograms, and technical reports.
* Support method verification, method transfer, process validation, cleaning validation, and troubleshooting activities.
* Ensure inspection readiness and actively support regulatory and customer audits.
* Supervise, train, mentor, and develop laboratory personnel while ensuring efficient workload distribution and resource utilization.
* Partner with QA, Manufacturing, Validation, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and R&D to meet business and compliance objectives.
  

**Required Qualifications & Experience**

* Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or related scientific discipline.
* Minimum 5+ years of pharmaceutical Quality Control experience with at least 3-5 years in a supervisory or managerial role.
* Strong experience supporting FDA-regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing environments.

  

**Technical Knowledge & Competencies**

* Hands-on experience in Finished Product and Stability sample testing within a pharmaceutical Quality Control laboratory. Experience with Raw Material testing is preferred.
* Strong knowledge of chromatographic techniques including assay testing, related substances (impurity profiling), degradation product analysis, and chromatographic purity determination using HPLC, UPLC, GC, and IC systems.
* Proficient in operation, troubleshooting, and lifecycle management of analytical instruments including HPLC, UPLC, GC, IC, Dissolution Testers, Karl Fischer, FTIR, UV-Vis, and XRPD.
* Thorough understanding of Oral Solid Dosage (OSD) product testing requirements and regulatory expectations.
* Strong technical expertise in pharmaceutical analytical methodologies, laboratory investigations, data review, and compliance-driven laboratory operations.
* Working knowledge of cGMP, GLP, GDP, Data Integrity requirements, USP, ICH guidelines, and FDA expectations.
* Experience with chromatography data systems and laboratory software including Empower, LabSolutions, Tiamo, and other computerized laboratory systems.
* Working knowledge of Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS), Electronic Laboratory Notebook (ELN), and Quality Management Systems such as TrackWise.
* Demonstrated experience in method execution, method troubleshooting, data review, technical assessments, and investigation management.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections and customer audits, including USFDA, customer, and corporate audits.
* Strong leadership, communication, documentation, decision-making, and problem-solving skills with the ability to effectively manage teams and collaborate across functions.

  

**GLOBAL COMPANY**

  

Cipla is a leading global pharmaceutical company, dedicated to high-quality, branded and generic medicines. We are trusted by healthcare professionals and patients across geographies. Over the last eight decades, we have strengthened our leadership in India’s pharmaceutical industry and fortified our promise of strengthening our global focus by consolidating and deepening our presence in the key markets of India, South Africa, the U.S., and other economies of the emerging world.

  

Cipla employs handpicked professionals not just for their knowledge and experience but for their zeal to make a difference to the world of healthcare. The company believes that our biggest assets are the employees, who lead us to prosperity and growth in the future. Driven by the vision, none shall be denied, Cipla’s focus has always been on making affordable, world-class medicines with a reputation for uncompromising quality standards across the world.

  

**CIPLA NEW YORK (INVAGEN PHARMACEUTICALS, INC.)**

  

About InvaGen Pharmaceuticals, a Cipla subsidiary InvaGen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is engaged in the development, manufacture, marketing, and distribution of generic prescription medicines with focus on a range of therapeutic areas, including cardiovascular, anti-infective, CNS, anti-inflammatory, anti-diabetic, and anti-depressants. The company was founded in 2003 and is based in Central Islip and Hauppauge, New York. As of February 18, 2016, InvaGen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. operates as a subsidiary of Cipla (EU) Limited.

**EEO Statement**

  

Cipla is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, genetic information, disability, or protected veteran status.

protected_roles.description:
**Company Summary: PuraGraft, a Young Innovations Company**

PuraGraft represents the leading manufacturers of biomaterial solutions for bone and tissue regeneration. No single material can suit all medical requirements and indications. However, through PuraGraft® you have access to the widest choices of products.

At Young Innovations, we foster a dynamic environment where team members make an impact every day as part of a collaborative, inclusive culture. Together, we serve the dental profession and their patients, united in our mission of achieving a Lifetime of Oral Health™

We embrace diverse perspectives and encourage bold thinking, challenging traditional approaches with a bias for action. Whether you’re looking to expand your skills or grow your career, Young is here to support your goals and continuous learning. At Young, YOU are at the core of what we do.

**Position Overview:**

Reporting to the VP Quality Regulatory Affairs, the Sr. Manager, Quality Assurance will be tasked with ensuring Quality standards are met or exceeded in all facets of the multi-site operation. He/she will partner internally in the development and implementation of new or adjusted quality standards, policies, and procedures, as required at Kingwood, TX and Scottsdale, AZ.

**You’ll like this role if:**

* You enjoy leading a team, solving complex quality challenges, and turning data into practical improvements. You take ownership of compliance and thrive in a hands-on role supporting quality standards across multiple sites.

**Why You’ll Love Working Here:**

* Medium sized company – not too big, not too small – just enough to get things done and see your impact.
* Did we say benefits? Full medical, dental, vision, 401k, parental leave, paid holidays, paid time off, short & long term disability insurance, employee assistance program, and more!
* Lead and inspire a dedicated team, build meaningful relationships, and help your employees grow and succeed.

**Who you’ll work with:**

* You’ll report to the VP of Quality & Regulatory Affairs and lead Quality Associates supporting our Kingwood, TX and Scottsdale, AZ operations.
* You’ll partner closely with QRA, Sourcing, Distribution, and Production teams to strengthen quality systems and drive continuous improvement.

**What You’ll Do:**

* Act as the site’s Sr. Quality and Compliance Leader, and when necessary, as the site’s Designated Management Representative to ensure compliance with all regulatory, corporate and facility requirements.
* Ensure compliance of two sites.
* Ensure outstanding Quality System performance via monitoring and measuring of process performance, and driving any appropriate action, including issuing and follow-up on activities required for sourcing, warehousing, and distributing pharmaceuticals.
* Supervise & Manage Quality Associates and develop culture of collaboration and cross-functional success within the department and business.
* Reviews and monitors Quality metrics and reports trends, to determine if there is a need to escalate issues to the management.
* Perform, review and monitor the Quality Management processes which include but is not limited to:
  + Ensure compliance with FDA, DEA and BOP requirements, including DSCSA traceability of pharmaceuticals.
  + Oversee Regulatory activities associated with distribution licensing, drug distribution reports, and permits for warehousing and distribution of controlled substances.
  + inspection and product release, label approval, calibration, warehousing controls, record retention, document control, training, control of non-conforming product, quarantined Products, control of access and drugs storage, including temperature monitoring.
  + Host and manage internal and external audits. Ensure the site’s readiness for assessments and lead implementation of corrective actions.
  + Effectively assess processes and identify opportunities for improvement.
  + Review, Analyze and Report Statistical findings through critical thought and storytelling of key findings and opportunities to all levels within a matrixed organization.
  + Partner with other departments to identify critical to quality metrics, and support the operationalization of monitoring and management to deliver improved performance across processes.
  + Create effective and compelling visual materials/presentations that support the process/product improvement impact to the organization and adequately represent the impact to quality, cost and time.
  + Define, track, and monitor key success measures associated with Quality Management Systems. Successfully deploy and support change management and appropriate training plans.
* Manage document control functions, including creation, review, and approval of procedures, work instructions and all other documentation for the Quality System.
* Manage the complaint handling system, including trending and review to identify opportunities for improvement.
* Manage the training of the Site, by maintaining the training log, tracking training completion of training by site personnel, creating training content and hosting group training as needed.
* Develop and host the Quarterly Management Review
* Manage the Recall process, from notification, tracking responses & expenses, reporting, and closure.
* Develop, refine, and/or maintain quality standards, policies, and procedures for the facility, including identifying, recommending, and fully implementing changes, in partnership with corporate QRA and local operations teams. Other duties as assigned

**What You’ll Bring:**

* Bachelor’s degree in technical field.
* Minimum of 3 Years of experience managing manufacturing and/or distribution of pharmaceuticals.
* Minimum of 3 Years of experience having direct responsibility for managing a Quality group.
* Direct experience managing FDA or DEA Inspections.
* Demonstrated proficiency in verbal and written communication in English, with the ability to convey information clearly, accurately, and professionally across all levels of the organization.

**Travel Requirements**

* Up to 15%

**Work Environment:**

**Office Environment**

This position is based in an office environment and is primarily sedentary in nature. It requires regular use of standard office equipment, including computers, phones, photocopiers, scanners, filing cabinets, and fax machines. Some roles may involve wearing a headset and sustained computer use for 8 or more hours per day. Employees may be required to sit, stand, or walk for extended periods, and occasional bending, lifting, or carrying items up to 50 pounds may be necessary.

**Manufacturing/Distribution Environment**

This position operates in a manufacturing plant environment. The role routinely involves working around machinery, equipment, and moving mechanical parts. The facility may be subject to varying temperatures, loud noise levels, and airborne particles such as dust or chemical fumes, depending on the area of the plant. This role may require periods of standing, sitting, or walking throughout the workday. Occasional bending, lifting, or carrying items up to 50 pounds may be necessary.

Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to finger, handle, control, or feel; reach with hands and arms and talk. Hearing abilities required for this environment include being able to clearly hear and respond to audible alarms, production equipment, forklifts, and other machinery to maintain a safe work environment. Individuals must be able to distinguish and understand verbal communication including instructions, safety warnings, and team discussions, sometimes in an environment with moderate to high background noise.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

**Your Role**

The Sr. Manager - Quality - Visual Inspection & Particulate Control provides strategic and technical Quality leadership for manufacturing and laboratory quality systems, with a focus on Visual Inspection and particulate matter control for injectable products. This role ensures that inspection programs, qualification/validation, particulate investigations, and associated controls are scientifically sound, risk-based, well documented, and aligned with regulatory requirements, compendial expectations, and the company Quality Management System.

**What You'll Be Doing**
------------------------

* Lead Quality oversight for manual, semi-automated, and automated visual inspection programs, ensuring inspection processes remain effective, compliant, and aligned with patient safety expectations.
* Develop and maintain risk-based particulate control strategies that strengthen defect prevention, improve manufacturing controls, and reduce product quality risks.
* Provide technical leadership for qualification and validation activities related to visual inspection systems, ensuring studies are scientifically sound, appropriately designed, and fully documented.
* Direct complex investigations involving visible particulate matter, inspection trends, and product quality events, driving objective root cause analysis and effective corrective actions.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Laboratory, and Quality teams to identify opportunities for process improvement, defect reduction, and continuous enhancement of inspection performance.
* Support regulatory inspections, customer audits, and health authority interactions by providing expertise, documentation, and responses related to visual inspection and particulate control programs.
* Establish and monitor quality performance metrics, trend analyses, and risk indicators to proactively identify emerging issues and ensure sustainable improvements.
  

  

**What You'll Bring**
---------------------

  
  

### **Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Pharmacy, Chemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related scientific or technical discipline.
* Typically 10+ years of progressive experience within pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical, medical device, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments, including significant Quality leadership responsibilities.
* Demonstrated expertise in visual inspection programs for injectable or sterile products, including inspection strategy, defect classification, qualification programs, and performance monitoring.
* Experience leading complex investigations, risk assessments, corrective and preventive action (CAPA) programs, validation activities, and regulatory inspection responses.
* Strong knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and applicable compendial requirements, including USP <790> and USP <1790>.
* Experience making science-based quality decisions involving product disposition, compliance risk management, and quality system effectiveness.
* Strong communication, collaboration, and influencing skills with the ability to build alignment across multiple functions while maintaining independent quality judgment.
* Leadership experience through direct people leadership, matrix leadership, or technical leadership roles.
  

  

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced degree in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Chemistry, Microbiology, Engineering, or a related discipline.
* Experience supporting commercial sterile manufacturing operations for injectable pharmaceutical products.
* Expertise in particulate characterization techniques, defect identification, and contamination control strategies.
* Experience implementing continuous improvement initiatives that improve inspection effectiveness, defect prevention, and process capability.
* Experience interacting directly with the FDA, Health Canada, EMA, or other global regulatory agencies.
* Certification or advanced training in Quality Risk Management, Lean Six Sigma, or related continuous improvement methodologies.

Vera Therapeutics is a commercial-stage biotechnology company focused on the pursuit of truth in science to transform medicine in autoimmune disease, starting with the kidney. Vera Therapeutics’ flagship commercial product is TRUTAKNATM (atacicept-vymj), a B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and A proliferation-inducing ligand *(*APRIL) inhibitor. Vera Therapeutics is evaluating multiple diseases where the reduction of autoantibodies through inhibition of BAFF and APRIL may prove clinically meaningful. Vera Therapeutics was founded in 2016 and is based in Brisbane, California. To learn more, visit www.veratx.com.

At Vera, our values are the cornerstone of our culture and guide how we work together every day. We lead with empathy, act with an owner’s mindset, demand clarity, work without fences, and execute with urgency because patients are counting on us. From how we hire and develop our people to how we advance rigorous science, we are building a team committed to transforming medicine in autoimmune diseases, starting with the kidney.

**Position Summary:**

The Vice President, Manufacturing Operations will report to the SVP Product Development and Manufacturing (PD&T) and will be responsible for leading the transition from a clinical-stage organization to an effective commercial manufacturing organization. As a key partner to the SVP PD&T, the candidate will lead and develop a best-in-class manufacturing and supply chain team that can collaboratively work across functions to enable commercial launch of our lead product into global markets. While working with internal teams, such as quality, regulatory, commercial, and finance, and external contract service providers, the individual is responsible for ensuring that the end-to-end supply chain is set up to meet the global commercial product demand with keen eye towards continuous process improvement.

**Responsibilities:**

* Leads the manufacturing and supply chain teams, providing leadership aligned with Vera values resulting in a high performing organization
* Contributes to the strategic leadership of Vera’s late-stage programs acting as a strong team player
* Participate in sales and operations planning (S&OP) and Product Development Teams representing the Product Development and Manufacturing function
* Create synergy and knowledge sharing to enable optimal production planning processes to balance supply/demand risks
* Serves as a single point of contact to manage end-to-end global supply chain and foster the needed supplier relationships to drive excellence using appropriate metrics
* Serves as a strategic thought leader to craft and manage commercial supply contracts with an eye towards life cycle extension programs
* Create, develop and manage necessary tools for end-to-end demand/supply planning
* Provide strategic direction, technical guidance, and long-range planning for late-stage programs: BLA-enabling studies through BLA submission, commercial launch, and sustaining operations
* Develop and manage department budgets and ensure fiscal responsibility for manufacturing operations
* Develop fit for purpose operational processes and systems to support supplier metrics and other tools to enable continuous improvement / process excellence
* Willingness to take on additional duties and responsibilities as assigned, and to adapt to changes in job scope as organizational needs evolve

**Qualifications:**

* Master's degree required. PhD preferred. Degree in Life Sciences or Engineering preferred
* 15+ years of relevant experience from biopharmaceutical manufacturing required.
* 5+ years of senior-level line management experience leading other leaders required
* Proven track record of creating business results
* Deep technical, operational, regulatory, strategic, and quality expertise, along with a proven track record of leading late-stage programs in innovative biotech or pharmaceutical organizations
* Experience with operating and navigating regulatory requirements including authoring and reviewing BLAs and interacting with regulatory authorities
* Solid understanding of drug development within the biopharmaceutical industry
* Experience within development and manufacturing of monoclonal antibodies or related field preferred
* Excellent interpersonal skills, collaborative leadership style
* Leads by example in recognizing and modeling Vera values
* Learning agility: ability to seek input, make connections, recognize patterns that lead to effective decision-making and action
* Proven ability to thoughtfully evaluate processes, identify opportunities for improvement and successfully execute on those plans
* Strong communication skills (oral & written); able to effectively interact with all levels internally and externally – able to tailor communications to the audience to achieve desired results
* Attention to detail with ability to move easily between hands-on work and strategic thinking
* Ability to multitask and prioritize.
* Strong leadership skills with a desire to nurture, train, and grow the existing finance group
* Demonstrated ability to influence and deliver results in a virtual (outsourced) environment

protected_roles.description:
**About David AI**
------------------

At David AI, our vision is to bring impactful AI into billions of lives through voice. Our mission is to help the world's leading AI companies build better voice models and agents. We're building the data and evaluation infrastructure behind those models.

Founded in 2024, we're a fast-growing Series B company backed by NVIDIA, Meritech, First Round, YC, and others, with ~70 people across San Francisco and New York City.

**About our Data Operations team**
----------------------------------

Our Data Operations team powers David AI's Data Factory, transforming raw audio into high-quality training datasets for leading AI labs. Our mandate is to spin up new data pipelines and run them at a massive scale.

This means starting from a model capability we want a model to unlock, experimenting with different shapes of data and collection strategies, and validating them with researchers. Once an approach works, we industrialize it, building pipelines that can process audio with reliability, quality, and efficiency. We are relentless operators who thrive in ambiguity, equally comfortable prototyping novel workflows as we are managing large-scale production systems.

**About this role**
-------------------

As **General Manager of Data Operations** at David AI, you will lead one of the most critical functions at David AI. You’ll own a major slice of our Data Factory: the engine that powers high-quality, scalable data production. You’ll lead the team responsible for building and scaling pipelines, from 0 1 experiments that unlock new model capabilities to 1 N industrialization that processes data reliably and efficiently.

**In this role, you will**
--------------------------

* Build and lead a team of Data Product Operations Leads, to spin up and scale data pipelines, from early experiments to production systems that generate high-quality audio data at scale.
* Act as a thought partner to executive leadership on how we can evolve and scale delivery capabilities in service of customer needs.
* Continuously monitor and improve pipeline health, spotting issues in sourcing, quality, or process early and owning solutions end-to-end.
* Use metrics to drive decisions, tracking throughput, quality, and cost to guide prioritization and identify where to scale or invest next.
* Work with researchers at leading AI labs to identify new model capabilities and turn them into concrete data workflows and project plans.
* Partner with our internal research team to design and test new data shapes that unlock frontier model capabilities.
* Own outcomes across functions, designing systems, managing execution, unblocking bottlenecks, and ensuring delivery at both prototype and production scale.

**Your background looks like**
------------------------------

* 5 to 10+ years of experience in high-ownership roles (e.g., founder, GM, COO, or strategy/ops at a venture-backed startup).
* Prior experience scaling large-scale operational efforts at high-growth startups or fast-paced companies.
* Technical fluency with data and operations; SQL proficiency required.
* Prior experience designing and scaling systems, processes, and teams across different customer segments and product lines.
* A relentless operator with high standards, bias to action, and strong attention to detail.
* Comfortable with ambiguity and rapid pace; thrives in a “build while flying” environment.
* Low-ego, collaborative, and mission-driven, focused on team and company success.

**Bonus points if you have**
----------------------------

* Experience in data, ML, or large-scale operations.
* Background in CS, industrial engineering, or similar.

**Benefits**
------------

* Unlimited PTO.
* Top-notch health, dental, and vision coverage with 100% coverage for most plans.
* FSA & HSA access.
* 401k access.
* Meals 2x daily through DoorDash + snacks and beverages available at the office.
* Unlimited company-sponsored Barry's classes.

**Visas**
---------

We sponsor international candidates across several visa types, including H-1B *transfers*, H-1B1, O-1, E-3, and TN. We also hire candidates on STEM OPT. If you’re on OPT, we’ll want to confirm you have a path to one of the visas listed above before your OPT ends. While we can’t guarantee any individual outcome, we’ve successfully sponsored teammates from all over the world.

Compensation Range: $205K - $235K
